# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Failure injection for the email ingestion path.

`test_get_email.py` covers the happy paths well. What it never does is hand the
ingester something broken: a MIME structure that does not parse the way the code
assumes, an attachment whose filename the filesystem cannot take, or a mailbox
connection that dies half way through a fetch. Every test here asserts how
`process_email` / `extract_email_metadata` degrade under one of those, so a
future change that turns a logged failure into a silent message drop fails loudly.

Several of the behaviours pinned below are pre-existing bugs, not regressions.
They behave identically on Django 4.2.30 and 5.2.17 (probed under both installed
trees), so per `docs/migration/pattern.md` step 6 they are asserted as they are
and written up in `docs/migration/reports/unit-7.md` rather than fixed inside a
migration diff. Each such test says so and names the line.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timezone as dt_timezone
import imaplib
import logging
import socket
from unittest import mock

from django.core.exceptions import SuspiciousFileOperation
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.test import override_settings, TestCase
from django.utils import timezone

import helpdesk.email
from helpdesk.email import (
    add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message,
    extract_email_metadata,
)
from helpdesk.models import FollowUpAttachment, Queue, Ticket


PLAIN_EMAIL = (
    "To: helpdesk@example.com\n"
    "From: sender@example.com\n"
    "Subject: Fetch me\n"
    "\n"
    "body text\n"
)


def build_email(*, subject="Hostile", extra_headers="", body=""):
    """An RFC822 string with the headers extract_email_metadata needs."""
    return (
        "From: sender@example.com\n"
        "To: helpdesk@example.com\n"
        f"Subject: {subject}\n"
        f"{extra_headers}"
        "\n"
        f"{body}"
    )


def email_with_attachment(filename):
    """A multipart/mixed with one text part and one attachment named `filename`."""
    return build_email(
        extra_headers='Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="BOUND"\n',
        body=(
            "--BOUND\n"
            "Content-Type: text/plain\n"
            "\n"
            "please find attached\n"
            "--BOUND\n"
            "Content-Type: application/octet-stream\n"
            f'Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="{filename}"\n'
            "\n"
            "payload\n"
            "--BOUND--\n"
        ),
    )


class SaveIncomingEmailMessageTests(TestCase):
    """`HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE` attaches the raw .eml.

    The timestamp in that filename is the only `timezone.localtime()` call in
    the library, and it is the one thing in this unit the 4.2 -> 5.2 move
    actually touched: Django 5.0 flipped the `USE_TZ` default from False to
    True, and `localtime()` rejects the naive datetime `now()` returns when
    `USE_TZ` is off.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Test", slug="test")
        self.logger = logging.getLogger("helpdesk")

    def test_nothing_is_attached_when_the_setting_is_off(self):
        files = []
        add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message(files, PLAIN_EMAIL)
        self.assertEqual([], files)

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True, USE_TZ=False)
    def test_the_raw_message_is_attached_when_use_tz_is_off(self):
        """Regression: this raised ValueError before the guard at email.py:783.

        `USE_TZ = False` is Django 4.2's default and still a supported setting on
        5.2, so an unguarded `timezone.localtime()` broke every install that had
        this feature turned on.
        """
        files = []
        add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message(files, PLAIN_EMAIL)

        self.assertEqual(1, len(files))
        self.assertEqual("text/plain", files[0].content_type)
        self.assertEqual(PLAIN_EMAIL.encode("utf-8"), files[0].read())

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True, USE_TZ=True)
    def test_the_raw_message_is_attached_when_use_tz_is_on(self):
        files = []
        add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message(files, PLAIN_EMAIL)

        self.assertEqual(1, len(files))
        self.assertEqual("text/plain", files[0].content_type)
        self.assertEqual(PLAIN_EMAIL.encode("utf-8"), files[0].read())

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True, USE_TZ=True)
    def test_the_filename_timestamp_is_local_wall_clock_not_utc(self):
        """23:30 UTC in a UTC+05:30 zone must stamp the next day at 05:00."""
        instant = datetime(2024, 3, 5, 23, 30, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc)
        files = []
        with mock.patch("django.utils.timezone.now", return_value=instant):
            with timezone.override("Asia/Kolkata"):
                add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message(files, PLAIN_EMAIL)

        self.assertEqual("original_message_06-03-2024_05:00.eml", files[0].name)

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True, USE_TZ=False)
    def test_a_naive_clock_is_stamped_as_is(self):
        """With USE_TZ off, now() is already local time and must not be shifted."""
        instant = datetime(2024, 3, 5, 23, 30)
        files = []
        with mock.patch("django.utils.timezone.now", return_value=instant):
            with timezone.override("Asia/Kolkata"):
                add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message(files, PLAIN_EMAIL)

        self.assertEqual("original_message_05-03-2024_23:30.eml", files[0].name)

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True)
    def test_an_ingested_message_keeps_a_copy_of_itself_as_an_attachment(self):
        """End to end, under whichever USE_TZ default the running Django has.

        That makes this test cover the naive branch on 4.2 and the aware branch
        on 5.2, and it is the test that fails on 4.2 without the guard.
        """
        ticket = extract_email_metadata(PLAIN_EMAIL, self.queue, self.logger)

        followup = ticket.followup_set.get()
        names = list(
            followup.followupattachment_set.values_list("filename", flat=True)
        )
        self.assertEqual(1, len(names), names)
        self.assertTrue(names[0].startswith("original_message_"), names[0])
        self.assertTrue(names[0].endswith(".eml"), names[0])

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True)
    def test_the_colon_in_the_stamped_name_survives_only_in_the_database(self):
        """Pre-existing quirk, not a migration change - see the unit 7 report.

        `_%d-%m-%Y_%H:%M` puts a colon in the name. Django's storage strips it
        via `get_valid_filename`, so the row and the file on disk disagree, and
        the name is not portable to a filesystem that rejects colons.
        """
        ticket = extract_email_metadata(PLAIN_EMAIL, self.queue, self.logger)
        attachment = FollowUpAttachment.objects.get(
            followup=ticket.followup_set.get()
        )

        self.assertIn(":", attachment.filename)
        self.assertNotIn(":", attachment.file.name)


class MalformedMimeTests(TestCase):
    """What the ingester does with MIME it cannot parse the way it assumes."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Test", slug="test")
        self.logger = logging.getLogger("helpdesk")

    def test_a_declared_boundary_that_never_appears_still_files_a_ticket(self):
        """The message is not dropped; it lands with a null description.

        `EmailMessage.get_body()` returns None for a multipart whose boundary is
        never seen, `extract_email_message_content` returns (None, None) for
        that, and the ticket is created with `description=None` rather than "".
        """
        message = build_email(
            subject="Broken boundary",
            extra_headers='Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="BOUND"\n',
            body="the boundary is never emitted\n",
        )

        ticket = extract_email_metadata(message, self.queue, self.logger)

        self.assertEqual("Broken boundary", ticket.title)
        self.assertIsNone(ticket.description)
        self.assertEqual("", ticket.followup_set.get().comment)

    def test_a_related_part_with_no_text_alternative_aborts_the_whole_queue(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/email.py:889` calls `.get_content_type()` on the result of a
        second `get_body()` without the None check the first one gets at :875,
        so a multipart/related holding only an image raises AttributeError.
        """
        message = build_email(
            subject="Related, image only",
            extra_headers='Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary="BOUND"\n',
            body=(
                "--BOUND\n"
                "Content-Type: image/png\n"
                "Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64\n"
                "\n"
                "iVBORw0KGgo=\n"
                "--BOUND--\n"
            ),
        )

        with self.assertRaises(AttributeError):
            extract_email_metadata(message, self.queue, self.logger)

        self.assertFalse(Ticket.objects.exists())

    def test_an_attachment_with_an_unregistered_media_type_is_named_part_1none(self):
        """Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/email.py:951` interpolates `mimetypes.guess_extension()` into an
        f-string without checking it for None, so an unknown media type yields
        the literal suffix "None".
        """
        message = build_email(
            subject="Unknown type",
            extra_headers='Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="BOUND"\n',
            body=(
                "--BOUND\n"
                "Content-Type: text/plain\n"
                "\n"
                "see attachment\n"
                "--BOUND\n"
                "Content-Type: application/x-not-a-registered-type\n"
                "\n"
                "payload\n"
                "--BOUND--\n"
            ),
        )

        ticket = extract_email_metadata(message, self.queue, self.logger)

        names = list(
            ticket.followup_set.get().followupattachment_set.values_list(
                "filename", flat=True
            )
        )
        self.assertIn("part-1None", names)


class HostileAttachmentFilenameTests(TestCase):
    """Attachment filenames the filesystem will not take verbatim."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Test", slug="test")
        self.logger = logging.getLogger("helpdesk")

    def attachment_of(self, ticket):
        return FollowUpAttachment.objects.get(followup=ticket.followup_set.get())

    def test_a_traversing_filename_cannot_escape_the_ticket_directory(self):
        """Django's `validate_file_name` reduces the name to its basename.

        Note that this also silently discards the "part-N_" prefix
        `process_as_attachment` adds, so two traversing attachments on one
        message would collide on name.
        """
        ticket = extract_email_metadata(
            email_with_attachment("../../etc/passwd"), self.queue, self.logger
        )
        attachment = self.attachment_of(ticket)

        self.assertEqual("passwd", attachment.filename)
        self.assertNotIn("..", attachment.file.name)
        self.assertTrue(
            attachment.file.name.startswith(
                f"helpdesk/attachments/{ticket.ticket_for_url}-{ticket.secret_key}/"
            ),
            attachment.file.name,
        )

    def test_a_filename_that_is_only_a_traversal_aborts_the_whole_queue(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        "../" leaves an empty basename, so Django refuses to derive a name and
        `process_as_attachment` (`helpdesk/email.py:957`) lets
        SuspiciousFileOperation out. One hostile message therefore stops the
        queue instead of losing one attachment.
        """
        with self.assertRaises(SuspiciousFileOperation):
            extract_email_metadata(
                email_with_attachment("../"), self.queue, self.logger
            )

        self.assertFalse(Ticket.objects.exists())

    def test_a_nul_byte_in_a_filename_is_stripped_on_disk_but_kept_in_the_row(self):
        """Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        Django's storage runs `get_valid_filename`, which drops the NUL, but
        `helpdesk/lib.py:162` writes the unsanitised name to the `filename`
        column. The two disagree, and on PostgreSQL the row write would raise.
        """
        ticket = extract_email_metadata(
            email_with_attachment("a\x00b.txt"), self.queue, self.logger
        )
        attachment = self.attachment_of(ticket)

        self.assertEqual("part-1_a\x00b.txt", attachment.filename)
        self.assertTrue(attachment.file.name.endswith("part-1_ab.txt"))

    def test_an_overlong_filename_is_truncated_to_what_the_filesystem_allows(self):
        ticket = extract_email_metadata(
            email_with_attachment("x" * 300 + ".txt"), self.queue, self.logger
        )
        attachment = self.attachment_of(ticket)

        self.assertEqual(255, len(attachment.filename))
        self.assertTrue(attachment.filename.endswith(".txt"))


class MailboxFetchTimeoutTests(TestCase):
    """A socket timeout part way through a fetch must not lose a message.

    `logging_type` is set so `process_email` keeps the queue logger's handlers
    and `assertLogs` can see the failure; with the blank default it clears them
    (`helpdesk/email.py:82-85`). No real socket is opened - the mailbox server is
    a Mock whose second fetch raises.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(
            title="Timeout",
            slug="timeout",
            allow_email_submission=True,
            email_box_host="0.0.0.1",
            email_box_port="49151",
            logging_type="error",
        )

    def pop3_server(self):
        server = mock.Mock()
        server.list = mock.Mock(
            return_value=(
                "+OK 2 messages",
                ("1 %d" % len(PLAIN_EMAIL), "2 %d" % len(PLAIN_EMAIL)),
            )
        )

        def retr(number):
            if number == "1":
                return ("+OK", PLAIN_EMAIL.split("\n"))
            raise socket.timeout("timed out")

        server.retr = mock.Mock(side_effect=retr)
        return server

    def imap_server(self):
        server = mock.Mock()
        server.search = mock.Mock(return_value=("OK", ("1 2",)))

        def fetch(number, _part):
            if number == "1":
                return ("OK", (("1", PLAIN_EMAIL),))
            raise socket.timeout("timed out")

        server.fetch = mock.Mock(side_effect=fetch)
        return server

    def assert_degraded(self, log_output):
        """The contract every transport shares when a fetch dies mid-run."""
        # The message that was read before the timeout became a real ticket.
        self.assertEqual(1, Ticket.objects.count())
        self.assertEqual("Fetch me", Ticket.objects.get().title)
        # The failure is logged rather than raised out of the command.
        self.assertIn(
            "ERROR:django.helpdesk.queue.timeout:Queue processing failed: "
            "timeout -- timed out",
            log_output,
        )
        # email_box_last_check is only advanced on success, so the next cron run
        # retries this queue rather than skipping past the unread message.
        self.queue.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertIsNone(self.queue.email_box_last_check)

    def test_a_pop3_timeout_mid_fetch_leaves_the_unread_message_on_the_server(self):
        Queue.objects.filter(pk=self.queue.pk).update(email_box_type="pop3")
        server = self.pop3_server()

        with mock.patch("helpdesk.email.poplib", autospec=True) as mocked_poplib:
            mocked_poplib.POP3 = mock.Mock(return_value=server)
            with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.timeout", "ERROR") as logs:
                call_command("get_email")

        self.assert_degraded(logs.output)
        # Only the message that produced a ticket was deleted from the mailbox.
        self.assertEqual([mock.call("1")], server.dele.call_args_list)
        # Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report: the
        # connection is never closed, because pop3_sync has no try/finally.
        self.assertFalse(server.quit.called)

    def test_an_imap_timeout_mid_fetch_leaves_the_unread_message_on_the_server(self):
        Queue.objects.filter(pk=self.queue.pk).update(email_box_type="imap")
        server = self.imap_server()
        # Patch only the IMAP4 class and keep the real exception classes on it,
        # so `except imaplib.IMAP4.error` in imap_sync means what it means in
        # production. Patching the whole imaplib module turns that clause into a
        # Mock attribute and Python raises TypeError instead of letting the
        # timeout through, which would pin the mock rather than the code.
        real_error, real_abort = imaplib.IMAP4.error, imaplib.IMAP4.abort

        with mock.patch("helpdesk.email.imaplib.IMAP4") as mocked_imap4:
            mocked_imap4.error = real_error
            mocked_imap4.abort = real_abort
            mocked_imap4.return_value = server
            with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.timeout", "ERROR") as logs:
                call_command("get_email")

        self.assert_degraded(logs.output)
        # Only the message that produced a ticket was flagged for deletion.
        self.assertEqual(
            [mock.call("1", "+FLAGS", "\\Deleted")], server.store.call_args_list
        )
        # Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report: expunge,
        # close and logout sit after the try block, so none of them run.
        self.assertFalse(server.logout.called)


class QueueSchedulingTests(TestCase):
    """`process_email`'s guard for a queue that has never been polled."""

    def test_a_queue_with_file_logging_and_no_previous_check_is_never_polled(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/email.py:100` only defaults `email_box_last_check` in the
        branch that has no file handler, so a queue with both `logging_type` and
        `logging_dir` set and a null `email_box_last_check` fails the comparison
        at :104 with a TypeError. It never advances, so it never recovers.
        """
        queue = Queue.objects.create(
            title="Filelog",
            slug="filelog",
            allow_email_submission=True,
            email_box_type="local",
            email_box_local_dir="/var/lib/mail/helpdesk/",
            logging_type="error",

#!/bin/bash
# PostToolUse hook: run only the test module that covers the edited file.
# Input is the hook JSON on stdin; the edited path is tool_input.file_path.
set -u
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
# Worktrees share the primary checkout's virtual environment.
MAIN="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.."
FILE=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("tool_input",{}).get("file_path",""))')
case "$FILE" in
  */helpdesk/tests/test_*.py) MOD="helpdesk.tests.$(basename "${FILE%.py}")" ;;
  */helpdesk/*.py)
    NAME=$(basename "${FILE%.py}")
    [ -f "helpdesk/tests/test_$NAME.py" ] || exit 0
    MOD="helpdesk.tests.test_$NAME" ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
PY="$MAIN/.venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$PY" ] || PY=python3
OUT=$($PY quicktest.py "$MOD" 2>&1); RC=$?
if [ $RC -ne 0 ]; then
  # Named failures when the runner got that far; otherwise the tail
  # (an import error or a traceback has no FAIL: line).
  SUMMARY=$(echo "$OUT" | grep -E '^(FAIL|ERROR):|^Ran |^FAILED')
  [ -n "$SUMMARY" ] || SUMMARY=$(echo "$OUT" | tail -15)
  echo "$SUMMARY" >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "$OUT" | grep -E '^Ran |^OK'

class TicketLookupSecretKeyTests(TestCase):
    """
    ``ViewTicket`` (``helpdesk/views/public.py:214``) is the only gate on a
    ticket for someone who is not logged in. With ``HELPDESK_VIEW_A_TICKET_PUBLIC``
    unset - the default here, and what ``helpdesk/settings.py`` ships - the
    ticket is only handed over for an exact ``submitter_email`` plus the
    ``secret_key`` from the notification email. Anything else falls through to
    ``SearchForTicketView``, which refuses with 403 while the setting is off.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Q1", slug="q1")
        self.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="Confidential subject",
            queue=self.queue,
            submitter_email="submitter@domain.com",
            description="Confidential body",
        )

    def lookup(self, **params):
        query = {
            "ticket": self.ticket.ticket_for_url,
            "email": self.ticket.submitter_email,
        }
        query.update(params)
        return self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:public_view"), query)

    def test_the_right_secret_key_opens_the_ticket(self):
        response = self.lookup(key=self.ticket.secret_key)

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertTemplateUsed(response, "helpdesk/public_view_ticket.html")
        self.assertEqual(response.context["ticket"], self.ticket)

    def test_a_wrong_secret_key_is_refused_and_discloses_nothing(self):
        response = self.lookup(key="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 403)
        self.assertNotContains(
            response, "Confidential subject", status_code=403
        )
        self.assertTemplateNotUsed(response, "helpdesk/public_view_ticket.html")

    def test_a_secret_key_that_is_not_even_a_uuid_is_refused(self):
        response = self.lookup(key="../../etc/passwd")

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 403)

    def test_an_empty_secret_key_is_refused(self):
        response = self.lookup()

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 403)

    def test_the_secret_key_is_compared_case_insensitively(self):
        """``secret_key__iexact`` in ``public.py:241``, not an exact match."""
        response = self.lookup(key=self.ticket.secret_key.upper())

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.context["ticket"], self.ticket)

    def test_the_right_secret_key_with_the_wrong_email_is_refused(self):
        response = self.lookup(
            email="someone.else@domain.com", key=self.ticket.secret_key
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 403)

    def test_the_submitter_email_is_compared_case_insensitively(self):
        response = self.lookup(
            email="SUBMITTER@DOMAIN.COM", key=self.ticket.secret_key
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)

    def test_a_ticket_id_that_is_not_a_number_is_refused_rather_than_raising(self):
        """
        ``Ticket.queue_and_id_from_query`` hands the trailing segment straight
        to ``Ticket.objects.get(id=...)``, so a non-numeric id raises
        ``ValueError`` rather than ``DoesNotExist``. ``public.py:243`` catches
        both.
        """
        response = self.lookup(ticket="q1-not-a-number", key=self.ticket.secret_key)

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 403)

    def test_a_ticket_that_does_not_exist_is_refused(self):
        response = self.lookup(
            ticket="q1-%s" % (self.ticket.id + 1000), key=self.ticket.secret_key
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 403)


@override_settings(HELPDESK_VIEW_A_TICKET_PUBLIC=True)
class TicketLookupWithoutSecretKeyTests(TestCase):
    """``HELPDESK_VIEW_A_TICKET_PUBLIC`` drops the secret key from the lookup."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Q1", slug="q1")
        self.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="Public subject",
            queue=self.queue,
            submitter_email="submitter@domain.com",
        )

    def test_a_wrong_secret_key_still_opens_the_ticket(self):
        """
        The key is not merely optional, it is not consulted at all: the branch
        at ``public.py:234-238`` looks the ticket up on id and email only.
        """
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:public_view"),
            {
                "ticket": self.ticket.ticket_for_url,
                "email": self.ticket.submitter_email,
                "key": "not-the-key",
            },
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.context["ticket"], self.ticket)

    def test_the_lookup_form_is_shown_when_neither_ticket_nor_email_is_given(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:public_view"))

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertTemplateUsed(response, "helpdesk/public_view_form.html")
        self.assertIs(response.context["ticket"], False)

    def test_a_lookup_missing_the_email_redisplays_the_form_without_its_error(self):
        """
        Pinned pre-existing bug, identical on 4.2 and 5.2.
        ``ViewTicket.get`` calls ``SearchForTicketView.as_view()(request, msg)``
        (``public.py:226-228`` and ``:244-246``), passing the message
        positionally. ``View.as_view``'s inner ``view()`` puts positional
        arguments in ``self.args``, and ``SearchForTicketView.get_context_data``
        reads ``kwargs.get("error_message")``, which is the URL keyword
        arguments - always empty here. So every "Missing ticket ID..." and
        "Invalid ticket ID..." message is dropped and the visitor gets a blank
        form back with no explanation. See docs/migration/reports/unit-5.md.
        """
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:public_view"),
            {"ticket": self.ticket.ticket_for_url},
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertTemplateUsed(response, "helpdesk/public_view_form.html")
        self.assertIsNone(response.context["error_message"])
        self.assertNotContains(response, "Missing ticket ID")

    def test_a_lookup_missing_the_ticket_redisplays_the_form(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:public_view"),
            {"email": self.ticket.submitter_email},
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertTemplateUsed(response, "helpdesk/public_view_form.html")
        self.assertEqual(response.context["email"], self.ticket.submitter_email)

    def test_a_ticket_that_does_not_exist_redisplays_the_form(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:public_view"),
            {
                "ticket": "q1-%s" % (self.ticket.id + 1000),
                "email": self.ticket.submitter_email,
            },
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertTemplateUsed(response, "helpdesk/public_view_form.html")

    def test_an_anonymous_visitor_gets_no_staff_redirect_target(self):
        """``get_next_url`` stays empty unless navigation or staff access applies."""
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:public_view"),
            {
                "ticket": self.ticket.ticket_for_url,
                "email": self.ticket.submitter_email,
            },
        )

class KBMissingAndForbiddenTests(TestCase):
    """
    ``helpdesk/views/kb.py`` is entirely public. These pin what it does with
    input that names nothing, and with a category the visitor may not see.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(
            title="Test queue", slug="test_queue", allow_public_submission=True
        )
        self.category = KBCategory.objects.create(
            title="Test Cat",
            slug="test_cat",
            description="This is a test category",
            queue=self.queue,
        )
        self.item = KBItem.objects.create(
            category=self.category, title="KBItem 1", question="What?", answer="A KB Item"
        )

    def test_a_category_slug_that_names_nothing_is_a_404(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:kb_category", args=("no_such_cat",)))

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    def test_the_category_slug_is_matched_case_insensitively(self):
        """``slug__iexact`` in ``kb.py:32``."""
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:kb_category", args=("TEST_CAT",)))

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.context["category"], self.category)

    def test_voting_on_a_kb_item_that_does_not_exist_is_a_404(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("helpdesk:kb_vote", args=(self.item.pk + 1000, "up"))
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    def test_a_category_that_is_not_public_is_a_404_for_an_anonymous_visitor(self):
        private = KBCategory.objects.create(
            title="Private Cat", slug="private_cat", description="Hidden", public=False
        )

        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:kb_category", args=(private.slug,))
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    def test_a_category_that_is_not_public_is_not_listed_on_the_index(self):
        KBCategory.objects.create(
            title="Private Cat", slug="private_cat", description="Hidden", public=False
        )

        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:kb_index"))

        self.assertContains(response, "This is a test category")
        self.assertNotContains(response, "Private Cat")

    def test_a_disabled_kb_item_is_not_offered_in_its_category(self):
        """``kb.py:35`` filters on ``enabled=True``."""
        disabled = KBItem.objects.create(
            category=self.category,
            title="Retired item",
            question="Old?",
            answer="Yes",
            enabled=False,
        )

        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:kb_category", args=(self.category.slug,))
        )

        self.assertNotIn(disabled, response.context["items"])
        self.assertIn(self.item, response.context["items"])
        self.assertNotContains(response, "Retired item")

    def test_a_kbitem_parameter_naming_no_item_selects_nothing(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:kb_category", args=(self.category.slug,))
            + "?kbitem=%s" % (self.item.pk + 1000)
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)

    def test_no_kbitem_parameter_leaves_the_selection_empty(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:kb_category", args=(self.category.slug,))
        )

        self.assertIsNone(response.context["selected_item"])

    def test_a_kbitem_parameter_that_is_not_a_number_raises(self):
        """
        Pinned pre-existing bug, identical on 4.2 and 5.2. ``kb.py:37-40``
        wraps ``int(selected_item)`` in ``except TypeError``, which only covers
        the ``None`` case. A non-numeric value raises ``ValueError`` and nobody
        catches it, so ``/kb/<slug>/?kbitem=abc`` - a URL anyone can type - is
        a 500. See docs/migration/reports/unit-5.md for the one-word fix.
        """
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.client.get(
                reverse("helpdesk:kb_category", args=(self.category.slug,))
                + "?kbitem=abc"
            )

    def test_the_kbitem_parameter_is_stripped_from_the_query_string_passed_on(self):
        """
        ``query_param_string`` is forwarded onto the "create a ticket" link, so
        the currently selected item must not be carried into it twice.
        """

        for an anonymous visitor. ``voted_by.filter(pk=None)`` is always empty,
        so the "have you already voted" guard never fires, and
        ``voted_by.add(None)`` writes nothing: Django's fast add path issues
        ``bulk_create(..., ignore_conflicts=True)``, so SQLite's

        """The URL pattern only matches ``up`` and ``down``."""
        response = self.client.post("/kb/%s/vote/sideways/" % self.item.pk)

"""
Coverage for ``helpdesk/validators.py`` and the parts of ``helpdesk/forms.py`` that are
not custom fields: the public attachment field, form media, the checklist forms and the
merge form.

``validate_file_extension`` is the only thing standing between a public submission and
an arbitrary file on disk, and nothing tested it directly before this module - the two
attachment tests that exist go through the staff update view.
"""

from unittest import mock

from django import forms
from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError
from django.core.files.uploadedfile import SimpleUploadedFile
from django.forms.models import inlineformset_factory
from django.test import SimpleTestCase, TestCase
from django.urls import reverse

from helpdesk import settings as helpdesk_settings
from helpdesk.forms import (
    ChecklistForm,
    ChecklistTemplateForm,
    CreateChecklistForm,
    EditTicketForm,
    FormControlDeleteFormSet,
    MultipleTicketSelectForm,
    PublicTicketForm,
)
from helpdesk.models import Checklist, ChecklistTask, Queue, Ticket
from helpdesk.validators import validate_file_extension


def upload(name):
    return SimpleUploadedFile(name, b"file content")


class ValidateFileExtensionTests(SimpleTestCase):
    def assert_accepted(self, name):
        self.assertIsNone(validate_file_extension(upload(name)))

    def assert_rejected(self, name, extension):
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError) as raised:
            validate_file_extension(upload(name))
        self.assertEqual(
            raised.exception.messages, ["Unsupported file extension: %s" % extension]
        )

    def test_an_extension_on_the_allow_list_is_accepted(self):
        for name in ["notes.txt", "guide.pdf", "letter.docx", "shot.png", "mail.eml"]:
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                self.assert_accepted(name)

    def test_an_extension_off_the_allow_list_is_rejected_by_name(self):
        for name, extension in [
            ("payload.exe", ".exe"),
            ("script.js", ".js"),
            ("archive.zip", ".zip"),
            ("sheet.ods", ".ods"),
        ]:
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                self.assert_rejected(name, extension)

    def test_the_check_is_case_insensitive(self):
        self.assert_accepted("NOTES.TXT")
        self.assert_accepted("Photo.PnG")
        self.assert_rejected("PAYLOAD.EXE", ".exe")

    def test_a_file_with_no_extension_is_allowed_through(self):
        # Deliberate: validators.py:26-28 lets an empty extension pass, and the TODO
        # there says so. A dotfile splits to ("<name>", "") and takes the same branch.
        self.assert_accepted("README")
        self.assert_accepted(".hidden")

    def test_a_bare_trailing_dot_is_allowed_through(self):
        # The second half of the same guard: ext == "." is accepted too.
        self.assert_accepted("report.")

    def test_only_the_last_suffix_is_inspected(self):
        # Pre-existing and unchanged by the migration: the check is name-based, so a
        # double extension is judged on its tail alone. "malware.exe.txt" is accepted
        # and "notes.tar.gz" is rejected. The TODO at validators.py:19 wants content
        # sniffing here; fixing it is a behaviour change, not a migration.
        self.assert_accepted("malware.exe.txt")
        self.assert_rejected("notes.tar.gz", ".gz")

    def test_the_allow_list_is_read_from_settings_at_call_time(self):
        with mock.patch.object(
            helpdesk_settings, "HELPDESK_VALID_EXTENSIONS", [".csv"]
        ):
            self.assert_accepted("data.csv")
            self.assert_rejected("notes.txt", ".txt")

    def test_turning_validation_off_accepts_anything_with_a_filename(self):
        with mock.patch.object(
            helpdesk_settings, "HELPDESK_VALIDATE_ATTACHMENT_TYPES", False
        ):
            self.assert_accepted("payload.exe")


class PublicAttachmentFieldTests(TestCase):
    """The attachment field on the public submission form carries the validator."""

    fixtures = ["emailtemplate.json"]

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(
            title="Attachment queue", slug="aq", allow_public_submission=True
        )

    def post_data(self, **extra):
        data = {
            "queue": self.queue.id,
            "title": "With an attachment",
            "submitter_email": "submitter@example.com",
            "body": "Body of the ticket",
            "priority": 3,
        }
        data.update(extra)
        return data

    def test_the_attachment_field_is_optional_and_validated(self):
        field = PublicTicketForm().fields["attachment"]
        self.assertIsInstance(field, forms.FileField)
        self.assertFalse(field.required)
        self.assertIn(validate_file_extension, field.validators)

    def test_a_submission_with_no_attachment_is_valid(self):
        form = PublicTicketForm(data=self.post_data())
        self.assertTrue(form.is_valid(), form.errors.as_data())

    def test_a_disallowed_attachment_stops_the_public_submission(self):
        form = PublicTicketForm(
            data=self.post_data(), files={"attachment": upload("payload.exe")}
        )
        self.assertFalse(form.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(
            form.errors["attachment"], ["Unsupported file extension: .exe"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(Ticket.objects.count(), 0)

    def test_the_public_page_redisplays_the_form_when_the_attachment_is_rejected(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("helpdesk:home"),
            dict(self.post_data(), attachment=upload("payload.exe")),
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(
            response.context["form"].errors["attachment"],
            ["Unsupported file extension: .exe"],
        )
        self.assertEqual(Ticket.objects.count(), 0)

    def test_an_allowed_attachment_reaches_the_ticket(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("helpdesk:home"),
            dict(self.post_data(), attachment=upload("notes.txt")),
            follow=True,
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        ticket = Ticket.objects.get()
        followup = ticket.followup_set.get()
        self.assertEqual(followup.followupattachment_set.get().filename, "notes.txt")


class FormMediaTests(SimpleTestCase):
    """
    Both ticket forms declare the same two scripts in the same order, and
    ``init_datetime_classes.js`` has to run after ``init_due_date.js``.

    Django 5.0 rewrote Media.merge on top of graphlib.TopologicalSorter
    (django/forms/widgets.py:206). The order it produces for these lists is the same
    as 4.2's stable topological sort, which is what these tests pin.
    """

    expected = [
        "/static/helpdesk/js/init_due_date.js",
        "/static/helpdesk/js/init_datetime_classes.js",
    ]

    def sources(self, media):
        return [str(script).split('"')[1] for script in media.render_js()]

    def test_the_public_form_lists_its_scripts_in_declaration_order(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.sources(PublicTicketForm().media), self.expected)

    def test_the_edit_form_lists_the_same_scripts_in_the_same_order(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.sources(EditTicketForm().media), self.expected)

    def test_merging_the_two_forms_media_neither_duplicates_nor_reorders(self):

class ChecklistFormTests(TestCase):
    def test_each_task_is_stripped_of_surrounding_whitespace(self):
        form = ChecklistTemplateForm(
            data={"name": "Template", "task_list": '["  first  ", "second\\t"]'}
        )
        self.assertTrue(form.is_valid(), form.errors.as_data())
        self.assertEqual(form.cleaned_data["task_list"], ["first", "second"])

    def test_a_template_with_no_tasks_is_rejected(self):
        form = ChecklistTemplateForm(data={"name": "Template", "task_list": "[]"})
        self.assertFalse(form.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(form.errors["task_list"], ["This field is required."])

    def test_a_task_list_that_is_not_json_is_rejected(self):
        form = ChecklistTemplateForm(data={"name": "Template", "task_list": "first"})
        self.assertFalse(form.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(form.errors["task_list"], ["Enter a valid JSON."])

    def test_a_json_string_task_list_is_split_into_characters(self):
        # Pre-existing quirk, identical on 4.2 and 5.2: clean_task_list maps over
        # whatever JSONField accepted, and a JSON string is iterable. The hidden input
        # is written by helpdesk/js, so only a hand-made POST gets here. Reported
        # rather than fixed - see docs/migration/reports/unit-9.md.
        form = ChecklistTemplateForm(data={"name": "Template", "task_list": '"abc"'})
        self.assertTrue(form.is_valid(), form.errors.as_data())
        self.assertEqual(form.cleaned_data["task_list"], ["a", "b", "c"])

    def test_a_numeric_task_list_raises_out_of_clean(self):
        # Same quirk, worse ending: map() over an int raises TypeError inside
        # clean_task_list, which is not a ValidationError, so it escapes the form and
        # becomes a 500 rather than a field error. Pinned, not fixed.
        form = ChecklistTemplateForm(data={"name": "Template", "task_list": "42"})
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            form.is_valid()

    def test_a_checklist_needs_a_name(self):
        form = ChecklistForm(data={"name": ""})
        self.assertFalse(form.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(form.errors["name"], ["This field is required."])

    def test_the_create_form_offers_the_template_before_the_name(self):
        # The template dropdown is rendered first on checklist_form.html, and field
        # order is what a bare render follows.

    def test_the_create_form_does_not_require_a_template(self):

class MultipleTicketSelectFormTests(TestCase):
    """``clean_tickets`` guards the merge view; only its happy path was covered."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Merge queue", slug="mq")
        self.other_queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Other queue", slug="oq")

    def make_tickets(self, count, queue=None):
        return [
            Ticket.objects.create(
                queue=queue or self.queue, title="Ticket %d" % index
            )
            for index in range(count)
        ]

    def test_two_tickets_from_one_queue_are_accepted(self):
        tickets = self.make_tickets(2)
        form = MultipleTicketSelectForm(
            data={"tickets": [ticket.id for ticket in tickets]}
        )
        self.assertTrue(form.is_valid(), form.errors.as_data())
        self.assertCountEqual(form.cleaned_data["tickets"], tickets)

    def test_a_single_ticket_is_not_a_merge(self):
        ticket = self.make_tickets(1)[0]
        form = MultipleTicketSelectForm(data={"tickets": [ticket.id]})
        self.assertFalse(form.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(form.errors["tickets"], ["Please choose at least 2 tickets."])

    def test_more_than_four_tickets_is_refused(self):
        tickets = self.make_tickets(5)
        form = MultipleTicketSelectForm(
            data={"tickets": [ticket.id for ticket in tickets]}
        )
        self.assertFalse(form.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(
            form.errors["tickets"], ["Impossible to merge more than 4 tickets..."]
        )

    def test_tickets_from_different_queues_cannot_be_merged(self):
        tickets = self.make_tickets(1) + self.make_tickets(1, queue=self.other_queue)
        form = MultipleTicketSelectForm(
            data={"tickets": [ticket.id for ticket in tickets]}
        )
        self.assertFalse(form.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(
            form.errors["tickets"],
            ["All selected tickets must share the same queue in order to be merged."],
        )

    def test_an_already_merged_ticket_is_not_selectable(self):
        target, merged = self.make_tickets(2)
        merged.merged_to = target
        merged.save()
        form = MultipleTicketSelectForm(data={"tickets": [target.id, merged.id]})
        self.assertFalse(form.is_valid())
        self.assertIn("valid choice", form.errors["tickets"][0])

Author: Waseem Khan <ceo@wazeem.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 2 15:28:36 2026 +0500

    Unit 2: keep helpdesk's own anonymous-access policy under Django 5.1+
    
    Django 5.1 added LoginRequiredMiddleware. It redirects every anonymous
    request unless the resolved view carries login_required = False, and it
    runs in process_view - before helpdesk's own gate. A host project that
    turns it on therefore never reaches protect_view, which silently turns
    HELPDESK_ANON_ACCESS_RAISES_404, HELPDESK_REDIRECT_TO_LOGIN_BY_DEFAULT
    and HELPDESK_PUBLIC_VIEW_PROTECTOR into dead config and hides the public
    ticket forms. helpdesk:login is worse: it bounces login -> login.
    
    protect_view now opts its wrapper out, which covers the five public entry
    points wired through it without touching urls.py, and views/login.py opts
    out the callable the URLconf actually resolves to (Django exempts
    auth_views.LoginView itself, but that is not what is routed).
    
    login_not_required is imported from Django on 5.1+ with a local fallback
    below it, so the attribute is set identically on 4.2 and the same tests
    assert the same guarantee on both. Applied after @wraps, which copies the
    wrapped view's __dict__ over the wrapper and would otherwise clobber it.
    
    The rest of the surface was checked against the installed 5.2 source
    rather than release notes: resolve_url and redirect_to_login are
    byte-identical to 4.2.30, and user_passes_test keeps the same sync
    contract despite its async rewrite.
    
    Tests go from 5 to 34. The five existing ones stop where the request
    leaves helpdesk, so the additions pick it up at the LoginView it hands
    off to (next round-trip, an off-host next rejected, bad credentials
    redisplayed), cover logout - which nothing exercised at all, and it has
    required POST since 4.1 - and cover the branches of protect_view,
    staff_member_required and superuser_required, including the two
    PermissionDenied ones. Three tests are version-gated and skip on 4.2;
    each has a non-gated sibling asserting the same guarantee there.

Unit 2: keep helpdesk's own anonymous-access policy under Django 5.1+

Django 5.1 added LoginRequiredMiddleware. It redirects every anonymous
request unless the resolved view carries login_required = False, and it
runs in process_view - before helpdesk's own gate. A host project that
turns it on therefore never reaches protect_view, which silently turns

ticket forms. helpdesk:login is worse: it bounces login -> login.

points wired through it without touching urls.py, and views/login.py opts
out the callable the URLconf actually resolves to (Django exempts
auth_views.LoginView itself, but that is not what is routed).

        )

High risk and notes that its existing 37 tests reach far fewer branches than
the file has. These tests cover the three framework surfaces that moved in
5.0/5.1 (formset rendering, auth redirects, CSRF) plus the paginator, the
``Case``/``When`` ordering, ``JsonResponse`` and ``ContentType`` call sites.

Every assertion here holds on both Django 4.2.30 and 5.2.17.

from django.urls import resolve, reverse

)

class StaffViewTestCase(TestCase):
    """A logged-in staff member, one queue and one ticket."""

        self.staff = User.objects.create_user(

        )
        self.staff.is_staff = True
        self.staff.save()
        self.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(

        self.client.login(username="staffer", password="pw")


class AnonymousAccessTests(TestCase):

    two fallback branches at staff.py:238-263, neither of which any existing
    test reaches.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        settings_obj = self.staff.usersettings_helpdesk
        settings_obj.tickets_per_page = 2
        settings_obj.save()
        for index in range(5):
            Ticket.objects.create(

class ChecklistFormsetTests(StaffViewTestCase):
    """edit_ticket_checklist builds the only formset in the module.

    Django 5.0 moved the default form renderer to ``div.html``. The formset is
    rendered field by field through helpdesk/templates/helpdesk/include/
    task_form_row.html rather than as a bare ``{{ formset }}``, so these
    assert on the contract the template guarantees - the management form, the
    field names, where the errors land - not on the surrounding markup.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.checklist = Checklist.objects.create(
            ticket=self.ticket, name="Pre-flight"
        )
        self.task = ChecklistTask.objects.create(
            checklist=self.checklist, description="Check the wing", position=1
        )
        self.url = reverse(
            "helpdesk:edit_ticket_checklist",
            kwargs={"ticket_id": self.ticket.id, "checklist_id": self.checklist.id},
        )

    def post_data(self, **overrides):
        data = {
            "name": self.checklist.name,
            "tasks-TOTAL_FORMS": "1",
            "tasks-INITIAL_FORMS": "1",
            "tasks-MIN_NUM_FORMS": "0",
            "tasks-MAX_NUM_FORMS": "1000",
            "tasks-0-id": str(self.task.id),
            "tasks-0-checklist": str(self.checklist.id),
            "tasks-0-description": self.task.description,
            "tasks-0-position": "1",
        }
        data.update(overrides)
        return data

    def test_the_page_renders_the_management_form_so_the_formset_round_trips(self):
        response = self.client.get(self.url)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        body = response.content.decode()
        for field in ("TOTAL_FORMS", "INITIAL_FORMS", "MIN_NUM_FORMS", "MAX_NUM_FORMS"):
            self.assertIn('name="tasks-%s"' % field, body)
        self.assertIn('name="tasks-0-description"', body)
        self.assertIn('name="tasks-0-position"', body)

    def test_a_valid_formset_saves_the_task_and_returns_to_the_ticket(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            self.url, self.post_data(**{"tasks-0-description": "Check both wings"})
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.task.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.task.description, "Check both wings")

    def test_an_invalid_formset_redisplays_the_page_and_saves_nothing(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            self.url, self.post_data(**{"tasks-0-description": ""})
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        formset = response.context["formset"]
        self.assertFalse(formset.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(
            formset.errors[0]["description"], ["This field is required."]
        )
        self.task.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.task.description, "Check the wing")

    def test_the_redisplayed_page_shows_the_error_next_to_the_field(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            self.url, self.post_data(**{"tasks-0-description": ""})
        )
        self.assertContains(response, "This field is required.")
        self.assertContains(response, 'name="tasks-0-description"')

    def test_an_invalid_checklist_name_redisplays_without_touching_the_tasks(self):
        response = self.client.post(self.url, self.post_data(name=""))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("name", response.context["form"].errors)
        self.checklist.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.checklist.name, "Pre-flight")

    def test_ticking_delete_removes_the_task(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            self.url, self.post_data(**{"tasks-0-DELETE": "on"})
        )
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.assertFalse(ChecklistTask.objects.filter(id=self.task.id).exists())

    def test_a_checklist_belonging_to_another_ticket_is_not_reachable(self):
        other = Ticket.objects.create(title="Other", queue=self.queue)
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "helpdesk:edit_ticket_checklist",
                kwargs={"ticket_id": other.id, "checklist_id": self.checklist.id},
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    without exempting the view from CSRF protection. Django 5.2 rewrote

    async paths; these pin that the sync behaviour is unchanged.

"""Failure injection for the email ingestion path.

`test_get_email.py` covers the happy paths. It never hands the ingester
something broken: MIME that does not parse the way the code assumes, an
attachment filename the filesystem cannot take, or a mailbox connection that
dies half way through a fetch. Each test here pins how `process_email` and
`extract_email_metadata` degrade under one of those, so a change that turns a
logged failure into a silent message drop fails loudly.

Several pinned behaviours are pre-existing bugs, not regressions: they are
identical on Django 4.2.30 and 5.2.17 under both installed trees, so per
`docs/migration/pattern.md` step 6 they are asserted as they are and written up
in `docs/migration/reports/unit-7.md` rather than changed inside a migration
diff. Each such test says so and names the line.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timezone as dt_timezone
import imaplib
import logging
from shutil import rmtree
import socket
from tempfile import mkdtemp
from unittest import mock

from django.core.exceptions import SuspiciousFileOperation
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.test import override_settings, TestCase
from django.utils import timezone

from helpdesk.email import (
    add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message,
    extract_email_metadata,
)
from helpdesk.models import FollowUpAttachment, Queue, Ticket


PLAIN_EMAIL = (
    "To: helpdesk@example.com\n"
    "From: sender@example.com\n"
    "Subject: Fetch me\n"
    "\n"
    "body text\n"
)

TEXT_PART = "Content-Type: text/plain\n\nplease find attached"


def build_email(subject, extra_headers="", body=""):
    """An RFC822 string carrying the headers extract_email_metadata needs."""
    return (
        "From: sender@example.com\n"
        "To: helpdesk@example.com\n"
        f"Subject: {subject}\n"
        f"{extra_headers}"
        "\n"
        f"{body}"
    )


def multipart_email(subject, *parts, sub_type="mixed"):
    """A multipart message whose parts are raw "headers\\n\\nbody" strings."""
    return build_email(
        subject,
        extra_headers=f'Content-Type: multipart/{sub_type}; boundary="BOUND"\n',
        body="".join(f"--BOUND\n{part}\n" for part in parts) + "--BOUND--\n",
    )


def email_with_attachment(filename):
    """One text part plus one attachment carrying `filename`."""
    return multipart_email(
        "Hostile",

class SaveIncomingEmailMessageTests(IngestTestCase):
    """`HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE` attaches the raw .eml.

    The timestamp in that filename is the only `timezone.localtime()` call in
    the library, and the one thing in this unit the 4.2 -> 5.2 move touched:
    Django 5.0 flipped the `USE_TZ` default from False to True, and
    `localtime()` rejects the naive datetime `now()` returns when `USE_TZ` is
    off.
    """

    def assert_raw_message_is_attached(self):
        files = []
        add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message(files, PLAIN_EMAIL)
        self.assertEqual(1, len(files))
        self.assertEqual("text/plain", files[0].content_type)
        self.assertEqual(PLAIN_EMAIL.encode("utf-8"), files[0].read())

    def stamped_name(self, instant):
        """The .eml name produced at `instant`, read in a UTC+05:30 zone."""
        files = []
        with mock.patch("django.utils.timezone.now", return_value=instant):
            with timezone.override("Asia/Kolkata"):
                add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message(files, PLAIN_EMAIL)
        return files[0].name

    def test_nothing_is_attached_when_the_setting_is_off(self):
        files = []
        add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message(files, PLAIN_EMAIL)
        self.assertEqual([], files)

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True, USE_TZ=False)
    def test_the_raw_message_is_attached_when_use_tz_is_off(self):
        """Regression: this raised ValueError before the guard at email.py:783.

        `USE_TZ = False` is Django 4.2's default and still a supported setting
        on 5.2, so the unguarded `timezone.localtime()` broke every install that
        had this feature turned on.
        """
        self.assert_raw_message_is_attached()

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True, USE_TZ=True)
    def test_the_raw_message_is_attached_when_use_tz_is_on(self):
        self.assert_raw_message_is_attached()

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True, USE_TZ=True)
    def test_the_filename_timestamp_is_local_wall_clock_not_utc(self):
        """23:30 UTC read in a UTC+05:30 zone must stamp the next day at 05:00."""
        self.assertEqual(
            "original_message_06-03-2024_05:00.eml",
            self.stamped_name(datetime(2024, 3, 5, 23, 30, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc)),
        )

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True, USE_TZ=False)
    def test_a_naive_clock_is_stamped_as_is(self):
        """With USE_TZ off, now() is already local time and must not be shifted."""
        self.assertEqual(
            "original_message_05-03-2024_23:30.eml",
            self.stamped_name(datetime(2024, 3, 5, 23, 30)),
        )

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True)
    def test_an_ingested_message_keeps_a_copy_of_itself_as_an_attachment(self):
        """End to end under whichever USE_TZ default the running Django has.

        So this covers the naive branch on 4.2 and the aware branch on 5.2, and
        it is the test that fails on 4.2 without the guard.
        """
        attachment = self.attachment_of(self.ingest(PLAIN_EMAIL))

        self.assertTrue(attachment.filename.startswith("original_message_"))
        self.assertTrue(attachment.filename.endswith(".eml"))

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE=True)
    def test_the_colon_in_the_stamped_name_survives_only_in_the_database(self):
        """Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `_%d-%m-%Y_%H:%M` puts a colon in the name. Django's storage strips it
        via `get_valid_filename`, so the row and the file on disk disagree, and
        the name is not portable to a filesystem that rejects colons.
        """
        attachment = self.attachment_of(self.ingest(PLAIN_EMAIL))

        self.assertIn(":", attachment.filename)
        self.assertNotIn(":", attachment.file.name)


class MalformedMimeTests(IngestTestCase):
    """What the ingester does with MIME it cannot parse the way it assumes."""

    def test_a_declared_boundary_that_never_appears_still_files_a_ticket(self):
        """The message is not dropped; it lands with a null description.

        `EmailMessage.get_body()` returns None for a multipart whose boundary is
        never seen, `extract_email_message_content` turns that into (None, None),
        and the ticket is created with `description=None` rather than "".
        """
        message = build_email(
            "Broken boundary",
            extra_headers='Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="BOUND"\n',
            body="the boundary is never emitted\n",
        )

        ticket = self.ingest(message)

        self.assertEqual("Broken boundary", ticket.title)
        self.assertIsNone(ticket.description)
        self.assertEqual("", ticket.followup_set.get().comment)

    def test_a_related_part_with_no_text_alternative_aborts_the_whole_queue(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/email.py:889` calls `.get_content_type()` on the result of a
        second `get_body()` without the None check the first one gets at :875,
        so a multipart/related holding only an image raises AttributeError.
        """
        message = multipart_email(
            "Related, image only",
            "Content-Type: image/png\nContent-Transfer-Encoding: base64\n"
            "\niVBORw0KGgo=",
            sub_type="related",
        )

        with self.assertRaises(AttributeError):
            self.ingest(message)

        self.assertFalse(Ticket.objects.exists())

    def test_an_attachment_with_an_unregistered_media_type_is_named_part_1none(self):
        """Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/email.py:951` interpolates `mimetypes.guess_extension()` into
        an f-string without checking it for None, so an unknown media type ends
        up with the literal suffix "None".
        """
        message = multipart_email(
            "Unknown type",
            TEXT_PART,
            "Content-Type: application/x-not-a-registered-type\n\npayload",
        )

        ticket = self.ingest(message)

        names = list(
            ticket.followup_set.get().followupattachment_set.values_list(
                "filename", flat=True
            )
        )
        self.assertIn("part-1None", names)


class HostileAttachmentFilenameTests(IngestTestCase):
    """Attachment filenames the filesystem will not take verbatim."""

    def test_a_traversing_filename_cannot_escape_the_ticket_directory(self):
        """Django's `validate_file_name` reduces the name to its basename.

        That also silently discards the "part-N_" prefix `process_as_attachment`
        adds, so two traversing attachments on one message collide on name.
        """
        ticket = self.ingest(email_with_attachment("../../etc/passwd"))
        attachment = self.attachment_of(ticket)

        self.assertEqual("passwd", attachment.filename)
        self.assertNotIn("..", attachment.file.name)
        self.assertTrue(
            attachment.file.name.startswith(
                f"helpdesk/attachments/{ticket.ticket_for_url}-{ticket.secret_key}/"
            ),
            attachment.file.name,
        )

    def test_a_filename_that_is_only_a_traversal_aborts_the_whole_queue(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        "../" leaves an empty basename, so Django refuses to derive a name and
        `process_as_attachment` (`helpdesk/email.py:957`) lets
        SuspiciousFileOperation out. One hostile message therefore stops the
        queue instead of costing one attachment.
        """
        with self.assertRaises(SuspiciousFileOperation):
            self.ingest(email_with_attachment("../"))

        self.assertFalse(Ticket.objects.exists())

    def test_a_nul_byte_in_a_filename_is_stripped_on_disk_but_kept_in_the_row(self):
        """Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        Django's storage runs `get_valid_filename`, which drops the NUL, but
        `helpdesk/lib.py:162` writes the unsanitised name to the `filename`
        column. The two disagree, and on PostgreSQL the row write would raise.
        """
        attachment = self.attachment_of(self.ingest(email_with_attachment("a\x00b.txt")))

        self.assertEqual("part-1_a\x00b.txt", attachment.filename)
        self.assertTrue(attachment.file.name.endswith("part-1_ab.txt"))

    def test_an_overlong_filename_is_truncated_to_what_the_filesystem_allows(self):
        ticket = self.ingest(email_with_attachment("x" * 300 + ".txt"))
        attachment = self.attachment_of(ticket)

        self.assertEqual(255, len(attachment.filename))
        self.assertTrue(attachment.filename.endswith(".txt"))


class MailboxFetchTimeoutTests(TestCase):
    """A socket timeout part way through a fetch must not lose a message.

    `logging_type` is set so `process_email` keeps the queue logger's handlers
    and `assertLogs` can see the failure; with the blank default it clears them
    (`helpdesk/email.py:82-85`). No real socket is opened - the mailbox server is
    a Mock whose second fetch raises.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(
            title="Timeout",
            slug="timeout",
            allow_email_submission=True,
            email_box_host="0.0.0.1",
            email_box_port="49151",
            logging_type="error",
        )

    def use_transport(self, box_type):
        Queue.objects.filter(pk=self.queue.pk).update(email_box_type=box_type)

    def assert_degraded(self, log_output):
        """The contract every transport shares when a fetch dies mid-run."""
        # The message read before the timeout became a real ticket.
        self.assertEqual(1, Ticket.objects.count())
        self.assertEqual("Fetch me", Ticket.objects.get().title)
        # The failure is logged with its stack trace rather than raised out of
        # the command, so the remaining queues still get their turn.
        self.assertEqual(1, len(log_output))
        self.assertEqual(
            "ERROR:django.helpdesk.queue.timeout:Queue processing failed: "
            "timeout -- timed out",
            log_output[0].splitlines()[0],
        )
        self.assertIn("TimeoutError: timed out", log_output[0])
        # email_box_last_check only advances on success, so the next cron run
        # retries this queue rather than skipping past the unread message.
        self.queue.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertIsNone(self.queue.email_box_last_check)

    def test_a_pop3_timeout_mid_fetch_leaves_the_unread_message_on_the_server(self):
        self.use_transport("pop3")
        server = mock.Mock()
        server.list = mock.Mock(
            return_value=(
                "+OK 2 messages",
                ("1 %d" % len(PLAIN_EMAIL), "2 %d" % len(PLAIN_EMAIL)),
            )
        )

        def retr(number):
            if number == "1":
                return ("+OK", PLAIN_EMAIL.split("\n"))
            raise socket.timeout("timed out")

        server.retr = mock.Mock(side_effect=retr)

        with mock.patch("helpdesk.email.poplib", autospec=True) as mocked_poplib:
            mocked_poplib.POP3 = mock.Mock(return_value=server)
            with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.timeout", "ERROR") as logs:
                call_command("get_email")

        self.assert_degraded(logs.output)
        # Only the message that produced a ticket was deleted from the mailbox.
        self.assertEqual([mock.call("1")], server.dele.call_args_list)
        # Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report: the
        # connection is never closed, because pop3_sync has no try/finally.
        self.assertFalse(server.quit.called)

    def test_an_imap_timeout_mid_fetch_leaves_the_unread_message_on_the_server(self):
        self.use_transport("imap")
        server = mock.Mock()
        server.search = mock.Mock(return_value=("OK", ("1 2",)))

        def fetch(number, _part):
            if number == "1":
                return ("OK", (("1", PLAIN_EMAIL),))
            raise socket.timeout("timed out")

        server.fetch = mock.Mock(side_effect=fetch)
        # Patch only the IMAP4 class and keep the real exception classes on it,
        # so `except imaplib.IMAP4.error` in imap_sync means what it means in
        # production. Patching the whole imaplib module turns that clause into a
        # Mock attribute and Python raises TypeError instead of letting the
        # timeout through, which would pin the mock rather than the code.
        real_error, real_abort = imaplib.IMAP4.error, imaplib.IMAP4.abort

        with mock.patch("helpdesk.email.imaplib.IMAP4") as mocked_imap4:
            mocked_imap4.error = real_error
            mocked_imap4.abort = real_abort
            mocked_imap4.return_value = server
            with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.timeout", "ERROR") as logs:
                call_command("get_email")

        self.assert_degraded(logs.output)
        # Only the message that produced a ticket was flagged for deletion.
        self.assertEqual(
            [mock.call("1", "+FLAGS", "\\Deleted")], server.store.call_args_list
        )
        # Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report: expunge,
        # close and logout sit after the try block, so none of them run.
        self.assertFalse(server.logout.called)


class QueueSchedulingTests(TestCase):
    """`process_email`'s guard for a queue that has never been polled."""

    def test_a_queue_with_file_logging_and_no_previous_check_is_never_polled(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/email.py:100` only defaults `email_box_last_check` in the
        branch that has no file handler, so a queue with both `logging_type` and
        `logging_dir` set and a null `email_box_last_check` fails the comparison
        at :104 with a TypeError. It never advances, so it never recovers.
        """
        logging_dir = mkdtemp()
        self.addCleanup(rmtree, logging_dir)
        queue = Queue.objects.create(
            title="Filelog",
            slug="filelog",
            allow_email_submission=True,
            email_box_type="local",
            email_box_local_dir="/var/lib/mail/helpdesk/",
            logging_type="error",
            logging_dir=logging_dir,
        )
        self.assertIsNone(queue.email_box_last_check)

        with mock.patch("os.listdir", return_value=[]):
            with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.filelog", "ERROR") as logs:
                call_command("get_email")

        self.assertIn(
            "Queue processing failed: filelog -- unsupported operand type(s) "
            "for +: 'NoneType' and 'datetime.timedelta'",
            logs.output[0],
        )
        queue.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertIsNone(queue.email_box_last_check)

# PostToolUse hook: run only the test module that covers the edited file.
# Input is the hook JSON on stdin; the edited path is tool_input.file_path.
set -u
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
# Worktrees share the primary checkout's virtual environment.

case "$FILE" in
  */helpdesk/tests/test_*.py) MOD="helpdesk.tests.$(basename "${FILE%.py}")" ;;
  */helpdesk/*.py)
    NAME=$(basename "${FILE%.py}")
    [ -f "helpdesk/tests/test_$NAME.py" ] || exit 0
    MOD="helpdesk.tests.test_$NAME" ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
PY="$MAIN/.venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$PY" ] || PY=python3
OUT=$($PY quicktest.py "$MOD" 2>&1); RC=$?

  SUMMARY=$(echo "$OUT" | grep -E '^(FAIL|ERROR):|^Ran |^FAILED')
  [ -n "$SUMMARY" ] || SUMMARY=$(echo "$OUT" | tail -15)
  echo "$SUMMARY" >&2
  exit 2
fi

class KBOptOutOfBlanketLoginRequirementTests(TestCase):
    """
    The knowledgebase URLs are wired into the URLconf bare - no
    ``protect_view``, which is what Unit 2 opted out of Django 5.1's
    LoginRequiredMiddleware. A host project turning that middleware on would
    hide the whole knowledgebase, public categories included, so the three
    read-only views declare the exemption themselves.
    """

    READ_ONLY_VIEW_NAMES = [
        ("helpdesk:kb_index", ()),
        ("helpdesk:kb_category", ("test_cat",)),
        ("helpdesk:kb_category_iframe", ("test_cat",)),
    ]

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Test queue", slug="test_queue")
        self.category = KBCategory.objects.create(
            title="Test Cat",
            slug="test_cat",
            description="This is a test category",
            queue=self.queue,
        )
        self.item = KBItem.objects.create(
            category=self.category, title="KBItem 1", question="What?", answer="A KB Item"
        )

    def test_the_read_only_knowledgebase_views_are_not_login_required(self):
        for url_name, args in self.READ_ONLY_VIEW_NAMES:
            with self.subTest(url_name=url_name):
                view = resolve(reverse(url_name, args=args)).func
                self.assertIs(getattr(view, "login_required", None), False)

    def test_voting_is_deliberately_left_login_required(self):
        """
        ``kb.vote`` writes, so it is the one view here that should stay behind
        a login. It carries no exemption, which means LoginRequiredMiddleware
        would guard it for a host project that enables the middleware.
        """
        view = resolve(reverse("helpdesk:kb_vote", args=(self.item.pk, "up"))).func

        self.assertIsNot(getattr(view, "login_required", None), False)

    @unittest.skipUnless(
        HAS_LOGIN_REQUIRED_MIDDLEWARE,
        "LoginRequiredMiddleware was added in Django 5.1.",
    )
    def test_the_knowledgebase_stays_readable_under_login_required_middleware(self):
        for url_name, args in self.READ_ONLY_VIEW_NAMES:
            with self.subTest(url_name=url_name):
                with self.settings(
                    MIDDLEWARE=[*settings.MIDDLEWARE, LOGIN_REQUIRED_MIDDLEWARE]
                ):
                    # A fresh Client each time: the middleware chain is built on
                    # a handler's first request, so a reused one keeps the old.
                    response = Client().get(reverse(url_name, args=args))

                self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
                self.assertContains(response, "Test Cat")
