"""Tests for the module-level helpers in ``helpdesk/query.py``.

Added by Unit 6 of the Django 4.2 -> 5.2 migration: the base64 query codec, the
free-text search translator, the datatables column tables, and the four quirks the
builder has today. Everything here behaves identically on Django 4.2.30 and 5.2.17
(probed under both installed trees), so the quirks are pinned as they are rather than
fixed, per ``docs/migration/pattern.md`` step 6. See
``docs/migration/reports/unit-6.md``.
"""

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.test import TestCase

from helpdesk.models import Queue, Ticket
from helpdesk.query import (
    DATATABLES_COLUMN_NUM_LOOKUP,
    DATATABLES_ORDER_COLUMN_CHOICES,
    __Query__,
    get_search_filter_args,
    query_from_base64,
    query_to_base64,
)
from helpdesk.user import HelpdeskUser


class Base64QueryTests(TestCase):
    """``query_to_base64`` / ``query_from_base64`` are the only way a saved search or a
    datatables URL carries a query, so the round trip is a wire contract."""

    def test_round_trip_preserves_the_query_dict(self):
        query = {
            "filtering": {"status__in": [1, 2]},
            "filtering_null": {"kbitem__isnull": True},
            "sorting": "created",
            "sortreverse": True,
            "search_string": "hello",
        }
        self.assertEqual(query_from_base64(query_to_base64(query)), query)

    def test_a_decoded_query_always_has_a_search_string(self):
        self.assertEqual(query_from_base64(query_to_base64({}))["search_string"], "")

    def test_a_null_search_string_decodes_to_the_empty_string(self):
        # staff.ticket_list seeds search_string with "", but a saved search written by
        # an older release can hold null; query_from_base64 normalises it so that
        # get_search_filter_args' "if not search" guard is reached with a str.
        encoded = query_to_base64({"search_string": None})
        self.assertEqual(query_from_base64(encoded)["search_string"], "")

    def test_the_payload_is_ascii_whatever_the_query_holds(self):
        # The encoded query is spliced into a URL path segment by
        # helpdesk:datatables_ticket_list, so a non-ASCII search term must not leak
        # out of the base64.
        encoded = query_to_base64({"search_string": "café naïve"})
        self.assertIsInstance(encoded, str)
        encoded.encode("ascii")
        self.assertEqual(query_from_base64(encoded)["search_string"], "café naïve")


class SearchFilterArgTests(TestCase):
    """``get_search_filter_args`` turns the free-text box into a Q object."""

    def test_an_empty_search_produces_an_empty_q(self):
        self.assertEqual(len(get_search_filter_args("").children), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(get_search_filter_args(None).children), 0)

    def test_a_queue_prefix_searches_only_the_queue_title(self):
        q = get_search_filter_args("queue:Support")
        self.assertEqual(q.children, [("queue__title__icontains", "Support")])

    def test_a_priority_prefix_searches_only_the_priority(self):
        q = get_search_filter_args("priority:1")
        self.assertEqual(q.children, [("priority__icontains", "1")])

    def test_a_plain_search_ors_across_all_ten_searchable_fields(self):
        q = get_search_filter_args("boom")
        self.assertEqual(q.connector, "OR")
        self.assertEqual(len(q.children), 10)
        self.assertEqual({value for _, value in q.children}, {"boom"})

    def test_or_joins_two_terms_into_one_flat_or(self):
        q = get_search_filter_args("alpha OR beta")
        self.assertEqual(q.connector, "OR")
        self.assertEqual(len(q.children), 20)
        self.assertEqual({value for _, value in q.children}, {"alpha", "beta"})

    def test_a_trailing_or_contributes_no_empty_term(self):
        # The "if not subsearch: continue" guard exists for this.
        self.assertEqual(len(get_search_filter_args("alpha OR ").children), 10)


class DatatablesColumnTableTests(TestCase):
    def test_the_column_number_lookup_is_the_inverse_of_the_choices(self):
        for number, name in DATATABLES_ORDER_COLUMN_CHOICES:
            self.assertEqual(DATATABLES_COLUMN_NUM_LOOKUP[name], number)

    def test_every_column_name_maps_to_a_real_ticket_field_or_annotation(self):
        concrete = {field.name for field in Ticket._meta.get_fields()}
        for _, name in DATATABLES_ORDER_COLUMN_CHOICES:
            with self.subTest(column=name):
                self.assertIn(name, concrete | {"last_followup"})


class QueryQuirkTests(TestCase):
    """Behaviour that is wrong but deliberate here.

    Each of these behaves the same on 4.2.30 and 5.2.17, so nothing about the Django
    upgrade forced a change, and changing one inside a migration diff would hide it from
    review. They are pinned so a later fix has to update an assertion that names the bug.
    """

    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.staff = get_user_model().objects.create_user(
            username="quirk-staff", is_staff=True, is_superuser=True
        )
        cls.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Quirk", slug="quirk")
        cls.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="quirk ticket", queue=cls.queue, description="d"
        )

    def huser(self):
        return HelpdeskUser(self.staff)

    def test_an_empty_query_params_dict_is_treated_as_no_query_params_at_all(self):
        # query.py:89 tests query_params for truthiness, not for None, so {} falls
        # through to query_from_base64(None). Every caller in helpdesk/views/staff.py
        # passes base64query, which is why this has never been hit in production.
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            __Query__(self.huser(), query_params={})

    def test_the_or_separator_is_matched_inside_words(self):
        # query.py:39 splits on the literal substring "OR", not on a word, so a search
        # for "FORM" becomes "F" OR "M" and matches almost every ticket.
        q = get_search_filter_args("FORM")
        self.assertEqual({value for _, value in q.children}, {"F", "M"})

        matched = __Query__(
            self.huser(), base64query=query_to_base64({"search_string": "FORM"})
        ).get()
        self.assertIn(self.ticket, matched)

    def test_ordering_by_the_commented_out_time_spent_column_raises_key_error(self):
        # Column 10 (time_spent) is commented out at query.py:69, but the datatables
        # front end still numbers the columns straight through, so a request ordering
        # by it is a 500 rather than a fallback.
        query = __Query__(self.huser(), base64query=query_to_base64({}))
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            query.get_datatables_context(**{"order[0][column]": ["10"]})

    def test_running_a_merged_null_filter_query_twice_drops_the_filters(self):
        # __run__ deletes the merged keys out of self.params (query.py:136 and :139),
        # which is the dict the Query holds, so the second run filters on nothing.
        params = {
            "filtering": {"kbitem__in": [1]},
            "filtering_null": {"kbitem__isnull": False},
        }
        query = __Query__(self.huser(), base64query=query_to_base64(params))
        self.assertEqual(list(query.get()), [])
        self.assertEqual(query.params["filtering"], {})
        self.assertEqual(query.params["filtering_null"], {})
        self.assertEqual(list(query.get()), [self.ticket])

"""Auth, permission and pagination branches of helpdesk/views/staff.py.

Unit 10 of the Django 4.2 -> 5.2 migration. The inventory rates this module
High risk and notes that its existing tests reach far fewer branches than the
file has. This module covers the login redirects, the permission-denied
branches and the paginator fallbacks; helpdesk/tests/test_staff_ticket_page.py
covers the ticket page, its checklist formset, CSRF and the JSON endpoints.

Every assertion here holds on both Django 4.2.30 and 5.2.17.
"""

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser
from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied
from django.test import RequestFactory, TestCase
from django.urls import resolve, reverse
from django.utils import timezone
from helpdesk import settings as helpdesk_settings
from helpdesk.models import Queue, Ticket
from helpdesk.query import query_to_base64
from helpdesk.user import HelpdeskUser
from helpdesk.views.staff import ticket_perm_check


User = get_user_model()


class StaffViewTestCase(TestCase):
    """A logged-in staff member, one queue and one ticket.

    Shared by this module and test_staff_ticket_page.py.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Staff Q", slug="staff-q")
        self.staff = User.objects.create_user(
            username="staffer", password="pw", email="staffer@example.com"
        )
        self.staff.is_staff = True
        self.staff.save()
        self.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="A ticket", queue=self.queue, status=Ticket.OPEN_STATUS
        )
        self.client.login(username="staffer", password="pw")


class AnonymousAccessTests(TestCase):
    """Every staff view sends an anonymous visitor to the login page, and the
    ``next`` parameter round-trips the URL that was asked for.

    Django 5.1 gave the ``user_passes_test`` wrapper ``login_url`` and
    ``redirect_field_name`` attributes so ``LoginRequiredMiddleware`` can read
    them, and 5.2 rewrote ``redirect_to_login`` to use ``urlsplit`` instead of
    ``urlparse``. Neither changes the redirect these assert on.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Anon Q", slug="anon-q")
        self.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(title="T", queue=self.queue)

    def assertRedirectsToLoginWithNext(self, url):
        response = self.client.get(url)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(
            response["Location"], "%s?next=%s" % (reverse("helpdesk:login"), url)
        )

    def test_dashboard_sends_an_anonymous_visitor_to_login(self):
        self.assertRedirectsToLoginWithNext(reverse("helpdesk:dashboard"))

    def test_ticket_page_sends_an_anonymous_visitor_to_login(self):
        self.assertRedirectsToLoginWithNext(
            reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id])
        )

    def test_report_index_sends_an_anonymous_visitor_to_login(self):
        self.assertRedirectsToLoginWithNext(reverse("helpdesk:report_index"))

    def test_datatables_endpoint_sends_an_anonymous_visitor_to_login(self):
        self.assertRedirectsToLoginWithNext(
            reverse(
                "helpdesk:datatables_ticket_list",
                kwargs={"query": query_to_base64({"search_string": ""})},
            )
        )

    def test_next_keeps_the_query_string_of_the_original_url(self):
        url = reverse("helpdesk:list")
        response = self.client.get(url, {"status": "1", "sort": "created"})
        self.assertEqual(
            response["Location"],
            "%s?next=%s%%3Fstatus%%3D1%%26sort%%3Dcreated"
            % (reverse("helpdesk:login"), url),
        )

    def test_staff_views_do_not_opt_out_of_login_required_middleware(self):
        """Django 5.1's opt-in LoginRequiredMiddleware skips a view only when
        ``view.login_required`` is False. No staff view may set it: they all
        belong behind a login, and helpdesk's public entry points are the ones
        that opt out (helpdesk/decorators.py:protect_view).
        """
        for name, args in (
            ("helpdesk:dashboard", []),
            ("helpdesk:list", []),
            ("helpdesk:view", [self.ticket.id]),
            ("helpdesk:report_index", []),
            ("helpdesk:email_ignore", []),
            ("helpdesk:user_settings", []),
        ):
            view = resolve(reverse(name, args=args)).func
            self.assertTrue(
                getattr(view, "login_required", True),
                "%s opted out of LoginRequiredMiddleware" % name,
            )


class PermissionDeniedTests(StaffViewTestCase):
    """The 403 and denied branches, which no existing test reaches."""

    def test_superuser_only_views_reject_a_plain_staff_member(self):
        for name in ("helpdesk:email_ignore", "helpdesk:email_ignore_add"):
            with self.subTest(view=name):
                self.assertEqual(self.client.get(reverse(name)).status_code, 403)

    def test_superuser_reaches_the_ignored_email_list(self):
        self.staff.is_superuser = True
        self.staff.save()
        self.assertEqual(
            self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:email_ignore")).status_code, 200
        )

    def test_followup_delete_silently_returns_a_non_superuser_to_the_ticket(self):
        """staff.py:387 redirects rather than raising, so a staff member who is
        not a superuser sees the ticket again and the follow-up survives."""
        followup = self.ticket.followup_set.create(title="Keep me", date=timezone.now())
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "helpdesk:followup_delete",
                kwargs={"ticket_id": self.ticket.id, "followup_id": followup.id},
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.assertTrue(self.ticket.followup_set.filter(id=followup.id).exists())

    def test_superuser_can_delete_a_followup(self):
        self.staff.is_superuser = True
        self.staff.save()
        followup = self.ticket.followup_set.create(
            title="Delete me", date=timezone.now()
        )
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "helpdesk:followup_delete",
                kwargs={"ticket_id": self.ticket.id, "followup_id": followup.id},
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.assertFalse(self.ticket.followup_set.filter(id=followup.id).exists())

    def test_ticket_perm_check_raises_for_a_user_outside_the_queue(self):
        """ticket_perm_check is the guard every ticket-scoped view calls."""
        outsider = User.objects.create_user(username="outsider", password="pw")
        request = RequestFactory().get("/")
        request.user = outsider
        with self.per_queue_permissions():
            with self.assertRaises(PermissionDenied):
                ticket_perm_check(request, self.ticket)

    def test_ticket_perm_check_denies_an_assignee_that_can_access_ticket_allows(self):
        """Pinned, not fixed - see docs/migration/reports/unit-10.md.

        ``ticket_perm_check`` (staff.py:282) tests ``can_access_queue`` first
        and raises, so it never reaches the ``can_access_ticket`` call on the
        next line. And ``can_access_ticket`` (user.py:78) returns True for the
        queue case before it ever looks at the assignee. So the assignee
        branch, which ``test_ticket_actions.test_can_access_ticket`` asserts on
        directly, cannot grant access through any view.
        """
        assignee = User.objects.create_user(username="assignee", password="pw")
        self.ticket.assigned_to = assignee
        self.ticket.save()
        request = RequestFactory().get("/")
        request.user = assignee
        with self.per_queue_permissions():
            self.assertTrue(HelpdeskUser(assignee).can_access_ticket(self.ticket))
            with self.assertRaises(PermissionDenied):
                ticket_perm_check(request, self.ticket)

    def test_a_staff_member_keeps_full_access_even_under_per_queue_permissions(self):
        """``has_full_access`` (user.py:56) returns True for any ``is_staff``
        user, so per-queue permissions narrow ``get_queues`` - and with it the
        dashboard and ticket list - without closing the ticket page itself."""
        with self.per_queue_permissions():
            huser = HelpdeskUser(self.staff)
            self.assertEqual(list(huser.get_queues()), [])
            self.assertTrue(huser.can_access_queue(self.queue))
            self.assertEqual(
                self.client.get(
                    reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id])
                ).status_code,
                200,
            )

    def test_anonymous_user_is_not_granted_full_access(self):
        self.assertFalse(HelpdeskUser(AnonymousUser()).has_full_access())

    def per_queue_permissions(self):
        return _OverrideHelpdeskSetting(
            "HELPDESK_ENABLE_PER_QUEUE_STAFF_PERMISSION", True
        )


class _OverrideHelpdeskSetting:
    """``helpdesk.settings`` is a plain module, so ``override_settings`` does
    not reach it; the existing suite mutates and restores it by hand."""

    def __init__(self, name, value):
        self.name = name
        self.value = value

    def __enter__(self):
        self.original = getattr(helpdesk_settings, self.name)
        setattr(helpdesk_settings, self.name, self.value)
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc_info):
        setattr(helpdesk_settings, self.name, self.original)
        return False


class DashboardPaginationTests(StaffViewTestCase):
    """``Paginator`` gained an ``error_messages`` argument in 5.2 but the three
    exceptions the dashboard catches are unchanged. These pin the two fallback
    branches at staff.py:238-263, neither of which any existing test reaches.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        user_settings = self.staff.usersettings_helpdesk
        user_settings.tickets_per_page = 2
        user_settings.save()
        for index in range(5):
            Ticket.objects.create(
                title="Assigned %d" % index,
                queue=self.queue,
                status=Ticket.OPEN_STATUS,
                assigned_to=self.staff,
            )

    def get_dashboard(self, **params):
        return self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:dashboard"), params)

    def test_first_page_holds_the_users_configured_page_size(self):
        page = self.get_dashboard().context["user_tickets"]
        self.assertEqual(len(page.object_list), 2)
        self.assertEqual(page.number, 1)
        self.assertEqual(page.paginator.num_pages, 3)

    def test_a_page_past_the_last_one_falls_back_to_the_last_page(self):
        page = self.get_dashboard(ut_page=99).context["user_tickets"]
        self.assertEqual(page.number, page.paginator.num_pages)
        self.assertEqual(len(page.object_list), 1)

    def test_a_non_integer_page_falls_back_to_the_first_page(self):
        page = self.get_dashboard(ut_page="not-a-page").context["user_tickets"]
        self.assertEqual(page.number, 1)

    def test_page_zero_falls_back_to_the_last_page(self):
        """Paginator raises EmptyPage, not PageNotAnInteger, for 0, so the
        dashboard lands on the last page rather than the first."""
        page = self.get_dashboard(ut_page=0).context["user_tickets"]
        self.assertEqual(page.number, page.paginator.num_pages)

    def test_an_empty_table_still_paginates_to_a_single_page(self):
        page = self.get_dashboard(utcr_page=99).context["user_tickets_closed_resolved"]
        self.assertEqual(page.number, 1)
        self.assertEqual(list(page.object_list), [])

    def test_tickets_the_user_reported_are_paginated_too(self):
        for index in range(3):
            Ticket.objects.create(
                title="Reported %d" % index,
                queue=self.queue,
                status=Ticket.OPEN_STATUS,
                submitter_email=self.staff.email,
            )
        page = self.get_dashboard(atrbcu_page=99).context[
            "all_tickets_reported_by_current_user"
        ]
        self.assertEqual(page.number, page.paginator.num_pages)
        self.assertEqual(page.paginator.count, 3)

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Direct tests for `helpdesk/lib.py`.

`lib.py` has no test module of its own today - `process_attachments` is reached
sideways from `test_attachments.py` and `text_is_spam` is reached by nothing at
all. Both are pinned here because they decide whether a submission's files and
body survive, and both currently drop things quietly.

Nothing here is a Django 4.2 -> 5.2 difference: every behaviour below is
identical under both installed trees. They are recorded per
`docs/migration/pattern.md` step 6 and written up in
`docs/migration/reports/unit-7.md`.
"""

import akismet
from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError
from django.core.files.uploadedfile import SimpleUploadedFile
from django.test import override_settings, RequestFactory, TestCase

from helpdesk.lib import process_attachments, text_is_spam
from helpdesk.models import FollowUp, Queue, Ticket


class TextIsSpamTests(TestCase):
    """`text_is_spam` gates every public ticket submission (`views/public.py:117`)."""

    def test_the_installed_akismet_no_longer_exposes_the_class_lib_imports(self):
        """The reason spam checking is dead. See the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/lib.py:103` does `from akismet import Akismet`. akismet 2.0
        replaced that class with `SyncClient` / `AsyncClient` plus a `Config`,
        so the import raises ImportError on every currently installable version.
        If this assertion ever fails, the pin below is stale and the report's
        finding has been fixed or the dependency floor has moved back.
        """
        self.assertFalse(hasattr(akismet, "Akismet"))
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(akismet, "SyncClient"))

    def test_spam_checking_is_off_and_the_import_failure_is_swallowed(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `except ImportError: return False` at `helpdesk/lib.py:104` was written
        for "akismet is not installed". It now also swallows "akismet is
        installed but its API moved", so the caller cannot tell a passing check
        from a check that never ran.
        """
        request = RequestFactory().post("/tickets/submit/")

        self.assertFalse(text_is_spam("cheap pills buy now", request))


class ProcessAttachmentsTests(TestCase):
    """What `process_attachments` saves, what it emails on, and what it drops."""

    def setUp(self):
        queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Test", slug="test")
        ticket = Ticket.objects.create(title="Ticket", queue=queue)
        self.followup = FollowUp.objects.create(ticket=ticket, title="Followup")

    def upload(self, name, content, content_type="text/plain"):
        return SimpleUploadedFile(name, content, content_type)

    def test_a_zero_byte_attachment_is_dropped_without_a_word(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/lib.py:159` guards the whole body with `if attached.size:`, so
        an empty file is neither saved nor reported. The submitter is told the
        upload succeeded.
        """
        attached = process_attachments(self.followup, [self.upload("empty.txt", b"")])

        self.assertEqual([], attached)
        self.assertFalse(self.followup.followupattachment_set.exists())

    @override_settings(HELPDESK_MAX_EMAIL_ATTACHMENT_SIZE=10)
    def test_a_file_over_the_email_cap_is_stored_but_not_returned_for_mailing(self):
        """The return value is the mail attachment list, not the saved list."""
        attached = process_attachments(
            self.followup,
            [
                self.upload("small.txt", b"tiny"),
                self.upload("big.txt", b"far more than ten bytes"),
            ],
        )

        self.assertEqual(["small.txt"], [name for name, _file in attached])
        self.assertEqual(
            {"small.txt", "big.txt"},
            set(
                self.followup.followupattachment_set.values_list("filename", flat=True)
            ),
        )

    def test_a_rejected_file_raises_after_the_valid_ones_are_saved(self):
        """One bad extension does not cost the caller the good files.

        The valid attachments are committed first and the errors are collected
        and raised together, which is what lets `create_object_from_email_message`
        log the failure and keep the ticket.
        """
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError) as raised:
            process_attachments(
                self.followup,
                [
                    self.upload("good.txt", b"fine"),
                    self.upload("bad.exe", b"nope", "application/octet-stream"),
                ],
            )

        self.assertIn("Unsupported file extension: .exe", str(raised.exception))
        self.assertEqual(
            ["good.txt"],
            list(
                self.followup.followupattachment_set.values_list("filename", flat=True)
            ),
        )

    def test_two_files_rejected_for_the_same_reason_raise_once(self):
        """`errors` is a set, so identical ValidationErrors collapse."""
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError) as raised:
            process_attachments(
                self.followup,
                [
                    self.upload("one.exe", b"nope", "application/octet-stream"),
                    self.upload("two.exe", b"nope", "application/octet-stream"),
                ],
            )

        self.assertEqual(1, len(raised.exception.error_list))

"""The ticket page and its neighbours in helpdesk/views/staff.py.

Unit 10 of the Django 4.2 -> 5.2 migration. Covers the checklist formset
(``inlineformset_factory``, whose default renderer moved to ``div.html`` in
Django 5.0), the two ``requires_csrf_token`` views, the two ``JsonResponse``
endpoints, and the ``Case``/``When`` and ``ContentType`` call sites inside
``view_ticket``.

Every assertion here holds on both Django 4.2.30 and 5.2.17.
"""

from django.test import Client, TestCase
from django.urls import resolve, reverse
from django.utils import timezone
from helpdesk.models import Checklist, ChecklistTask, Ticket, TicketDependency
from helpdesk.query import query_to_base64
from helpdesk.tests.test_staff_views import StaffViewTestCase
import json


class ChecklistFormsetTests(StaffViewTestCase):
    """``edit_ticket_checklist`` builds the only formset in the module.

    Django 5.0 moved the default form renderer from ``table.html`` to
    ``div.html``, and ``formset_factory`` stopped baking a renderer into the
    generated class. Neither reaches this page: it renders the formset field by
    field through helpdesk/templates/helpdesk/include/task_form_row.html rather
    than as a bare ``{{ formset }}``. These assert what the template
    guarantees - the management form, the field names, where the errors land -
    not the surrounding markup.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.checklist = Checklist.objects.create(ticket=self.ticket, name="Pre-flight")
        self.task = ChecklistTask.objects.create(
            checklist=self.checklist, description="Check the wing", position=1
        )
        self.url = reverse(
            "helpdesk:edit_ticket_checklist",
            kwargs={"ticket_id": self.ticket.id, "checklist_id": self.checklist.id},
        )

    def post_data(self, **overrides):
        data = {
            "name": self.checklist.name,
            "tasks-TOTAL_FORMS": "1",
            "tasks-INITIAL_FORMS": "1",
            "tasks-MIN_NUM_FORMS": "0",
            "tasks-MAX_NUM_FORMS": "1000",
            "tasks-0-id": str(self.task.id),
            "tasks-0-checklist": str(self.checklist.id),
            "tasks-0-description": self.task.description,
            "tasks-0-position": "1",
        }
        data.update(overrides)
        return data

    def test_the_page_renders_the_management_form_so_the_formset_round_trips(self):
        response = self.client.get(self.url)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        body = response.content.decode()
        for field in ("TOTAL_FORMS", "INITIAL_FORMS", "MIN_NUM_FORMS", "MAX_NUM_FORMS"):
            self.assertIn('name="tasks-%s"' % field, body)
        self.assertIn('name="tasks-0-description"', body)
        self.assertIn('name="tasks-0-position"', body)

    def test_a_valid_formset_saves_the_task_and_returns_to_the_ticket(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            self.url, self.post_data(**{"tasks-0-description": "Check both wings"})
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.task.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.task.description, "Check both wings")

    def test_an_invalid_formset_redisplays_the_page_and_saves_nothing(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            self.url, self.post_data(**{"tasks-0-description": ""})
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        formset = response.context["formset"]
        self.assertFalse(formset.is_valid())
        self.assertEqual(formset.errors[0]["description"], ["This field is required."])
        self.task.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.task.description, "Check the wing")

    def test_the_redisplayed_page_shows_the_error_and_the_field_it_belongs_to(self):
        response = self.client.post(
            self.url, self.post_data(**{"tasks-0-description": ""})
        )
        self.assertContains(response, "This field is required.")
        self.assertContains(response, 'name="tasks-0-description"')

    def test_an_invalid_checklist_name_redisplays_without_touching_the_tasks(self):
        response = self.client.post(self.url, self.post_data(name=""))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("name", response.context["form"].errors)
        self.checklist.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.checklist.name, "Pre-flight")

    def test_a_missing_management_form_leaves_the_tasks_alone(self):
        """A bare POST has no management form, so the formset is invalid and
        the page is redisplayed rather than the tasks being wiped."""
        response = self.client.post(self.url, {"name": "Renamed"})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertTrue(ChecklistTask.objects.filter(id=self.task.id).exists())

    def test_ticking_delete_removes_the_task(self):
        response = self.client.post(self.url, self.post_data(**{"tasks-0-DELETE": "on"}))
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.assertFalse(ChecklistTask.objects.filter(id=self.task.id).exists())

    def test_the_delete_checkbox_carries_the_bootstrap_class_the_page_styles(self):
        """``FormControlDeleteFormSet`` sets ``deletion_widget``; the 5.0
        renderer change must not drop the attribute the stylesheet keys on."""
        response = self.client.get(self.url)
        self.assertContains(response, 'name="tasks-0-DELETE"')
        self.assertIn(
            "form-control",
            response.context["formset"].forms[0].fields["DELETE"].widget.attrs["class"],
        )

    def test_a_checklist_belonging_to_another_ticket_is_not_reachable(self):
        other = Ticket.objects.create(title="Other", queue=self.queue)
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "helpdesk:edit_ticket_checklist",
                kwargs={"ticket_id": other.id, "checklist_id": self.checklist.id},
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    def test_deleting_a_checklist_needs_a_post_and_then_returns_to_the_ticket(self):
        url = reverse(
            "helpdesk:delete_ticket_checklist",
            kwargs={"ticket_id": self.ticket.id, "checklist_id": self.checklist.id},
        )
        self.assertEqual(self.client.get(url).status_code, 200)
        self.assertTrue(Checklist.objects.filter(id=self.checklist.id).exists())

        response = self.client.post(url)
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.assertFalse(Checklist.objects.filter(id=self.checklist.id).exists())


class CsrfTests(StaffViewTestCase):
    """``requires_csrf_token`` makes a token available to the response without
    exempting the view from CSRF protection. Django 5.2 rewrote
    ``decorator_from_middleware`` (utils/decorators.py) to split the sync and
    async paths; these pin that the sync path behaves as it did.
    """

    def test_hold_and_unhold_toggle_the_flag_and_return_to_the_ticket(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:hold", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.ticket.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertTrue(self.ticket.on_hold)

        self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:unhold", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        self.ticket.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertFalse(self.ticket.on_hold)

    def test_holding_a_ticket_records_a_followup_naming_the_action(self):
        self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:hold", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        self.assertEqual(
            self.ticket.followup_set.latest("id").title, "Ticket placed on hold"
        )
        self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:unhold", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        self.assertEqual(
            self.ticket.followup_set.latest("id").title, "Ticket taken off hold"
        )

    def test_requires_csrf_token_puts_a_token_on_the_request(self):
        """The point of the decorator: an error template rendered for this
        request can still emit ``{% csrf_token %}``."""
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:hold", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        self.assertIn("CSRF_COOKIE", response.wsgi_request.META)

    def test_requires_csrf_token_does_not_exempt_the_view(self):
        view = resolve(reverse("helpdesk:hold", args=[self.ticket.id])).func
        self.assertFalse(getattr(view, "csrf_exempt", False))

    def test_a_post_without_a_csrf_token_is_still_rejected(self):
        strict = Client(enforce_csrf_checks=True)
        strict.login(username="staffer", password="pw")
        response = strict.post(
            reverse("helpdesk:update", kwargs={"ticket_id": self.ticket.id}),
            {"title": self.ticket.title, "priority": self.ticket.priority},
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 403)


class JsonEndpointTests(StaffViewTestCase):
    """The two ``JsonResponse`` endpoints. ``JsonResponse`` is unchanged
    between 4.2 and 5.2 (probed); what these pin is that the staff decorator
    stack plus DRF's ``api_view`` still let a JSON request reach it.
    """

    def encoded_query(self):
        return query_to_base64(
            {
                "filtering": {},
                "filtering_null": {},
                "sorting": "created",
                "sortreverse": False,
                "search_string": "",
            }
        )

    def test_datatables_endpoint_returns_the_shape_the_table_expects(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "helpdesk:datatables_ticket_list",
                kwargs={"query": self.encoded_query()},
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response["Content-Type"], "application/json")
        payload = json.loads(response.content)
        self.assertEqual(payload["recordsTotal"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(payload["data"][0]["id"], self.ticket.id)

    def test_timeline_endpoint_returns_one_event_per_followup(self):
        self.ticket.followup_set.create(
            title="Opened", date=timezone.now(), comment="hello"
        )
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "helpdesk:timeline_ticket_list", kwargs={"query": self.encoded_query()}
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        payload = json.loads(response.content)
        self.assertEqual(len(payload["events"]), 1)
        self.assertIn("Opened", payload["events"][0]["text"]["headline"])


class TicketPageQueryTests(StaffViewTestCase):
    """``view_ticket``'s two ORM call sites: the ``Case``/``When`` ranking of
    dependencies (staff.py:467) and the ``ContentType`` lookup that builds the
    submitter's admin link (staff.py:443).
    """

    def test_open_dependencies_are_listed_before_closed_ones(self):
        closed = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="Closed dep", queue=self.queue, status=Ticket.CLOSED_STATUS
        )
        open_ = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="Open dep", queue=self.queue, status=Ticket.OPEN_STATUS
        )
        TicketDependency.objects.create(ticket=self.ticket, depends_on=closed)
        TicketDependency.objects.create(ticket=self.ticket, depends_on=open_)

        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        ranked = list(response.context["dependencies"])
        self.assertEqual(
            [dep.depends_on.title for dep in ranked], ["Open dep", "Closed dep"]
        )
        self.assertEqual([dep.rank for dep in ranked], [1, 2])

    def test_a_submitter_with_an_account_gets_a_link_to_their_admin_page(self):
        self.ticket.submitter_email = self.staff.email
        self.ticket.save()
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        self.assertEqual(
            response.context["submitter_userprofile_url"],
            reverse("admin:auth_user_change", kwargs={"object_id": self.staff.id}),
        )

    def test_a_submitter_without_an_account_gets_no_admin_link(self):
        self.ticket.submitter_email = "nobody@example.com"
        self.ticket.save()
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        self.assertIsNone(response.context["submitter_userprofile_url"])

    def test_taking_a_ticket_from_the_ticket_page_assigns_it_and_redirects_back(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]), {"take": "1"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.ticket.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.ticket.assigned_to, self.staff)

    def test_subscribing_from_the_ticket_page_adds_the_user_once(self):
        url = reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id])
        self.client.get(url, {"subscribe": "1"})
        self.assertEqual(self.ticket.ticketcc_set.filter(user=self.staff).count(), 1)
        self.client.get(url, {"subscribe": "1"})
        self.assertEqual(self.ticket.ticketcc_set.filter(user=self.staff).count(), 1)

    def test_closing_a_resolved_ticket_from_the_ticket_page_closes_it(self):
        self.ticket.status = Ticket.RESOLVED_STATUS
        self.ticket.save()
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]), {"close": "1"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.ticket.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.ticket.status, Ticket.CLOSED_STATUS)

    def test_close_is_ignored_on_a_ticket_that_is_not_resolved(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]), {"close": "1"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.ticket.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.ticket.status, Ticket.OPEN_STATUS)

"""What the ticket API guarantees about datetimes, under either ``USE_TZ``.

Added by Unit 6 of the Django 4.2 -> 5.2 migration.

These tests do **not** replace the three failing assertions in ``test_api.py``
(``test_create_api_ticket_with_basic_auth:149``, ``test_edit_api_ticket:188``,
``test_create_api_ticket_with_custom_fields:287``). Those three are still red on
Django 5.2 and are reported, not hidden, in ``docs/migration/reports/unit-6.md``:
they assert a naive ``datetime`` and a ``Z``-less ISO string, which only hold while
``settings.USE_TZ`` is ``False``, and ``quicktest.py`` never declares it, so the value
changed under the suite when Django 5.2 flipped the global default.

What is pinned here is the part of the contract that is true either way: the API stores
and returns the instant the client sent. A test written like this would have caught the
flip as a configuration change instead of as three mystery failures, which is the only
reason it is worth adding.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone as py_timezone

from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.utils import timezone
from django.utils.dateparse import parse_datetime
from rest_framework.status import HTTP_200_OK, HTTP_201_CREATED
from rest_framework.test import APITestCase

from helpdesk.models import Queue, Ticket


def wall_clock(value):
    """The wall clock ``value`` shows in the project's timezone.

    With ``USE_TZ`` on, the ORM hands back an aware UTC datetime; with it off, the same
    instant comes back naive in the project's timezone. Both spell the same wall clock,
    and the wall clock is what the API's callers read, so that is what is asserted.
    """
    if value is None:
        return None
    if timezone.is_aware(value):
        value = timezone.localtime(value)
    return value.replace(tzinfo=None)


class TicketDueDateContractTests(APITestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Test Queue", slug="test-queue")

        response = self.client.post(

            {

                "title": "Wall clock",
                "description": "d",
                "priority": 3,
                "due_date": "2022-04-10T15:06:00",
            },
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, HTTP_201_CREATED)
        stored = Ticket.objects.get(pk=response.data["id"]).due_date
        self.assertEqual(wall_clock(stored), datetime(2022, 4, 10, 15, 6))

    def test_a_due_date_posted_with_an_offset_is_stored_as_the_same_instant(self):
        # 17:06+02:00 is 15:06 UTC, and TIME_ZONE is UTC under quicktest.py.
        response = self.client.post(
            "/api/tickets/",
            {
                "queue": self.queue.id,
                "title": "Offset",
                "description": "d",
                "priority": 3,
                "due_date": "2022-04-10T17:06:00+02:00",

        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, HTTP_201_CREATED)

        self.assertEqual(wall_clock(stored), datetime(2022, 4, 10, 15, 6))

        self.assertEqual(wall_clock(ticket.due_date), datetime(2022, 4, 10, 15, 6))

    def test_a_ticket_with_no_due_date_serializes_it_as_null(self):
        ticket = Ticket.objects.create(queue=self.queue, title="No due date")

        )

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Failure injection at the mailbox connection, not the message.

`test_get_email.py` mocks POP3 and IMAP servers that always answer. These tests
mock ones that stop answering part way through, or refuse the login, and pin how
far `process_email` gets afterwards. The point in every case is the same: a
message must never be deleted from the mailbox without a ticket to show for it,
and a broken queue must not take the rest of the run down with it.

No real socket is opened anywhere here and no test sleeps; the servers are Mocks
whose methods raise.

Everything pinned below is a pre-existing bug or quirk, identical on Django
4.2.30 and 5.2.17, recorded per `docs/migration/pattern.md` step 6 and written
up in `docs/migration/reports/unit-7.md`.
"""

import imaplib
from shutil import rmtree
import socket
from tempfile import mkdtemp
from unittest import mock

from django.core.management import call_command
from django.test import TestCase

from helpdesk.models import Queue, Ticket
from helpdesk.tests.test_get_email_failures import PLAIN_EMAIL


def patched_imap4(server):
    """Patch only the IMAP4 class, keeping its real exception classes.

    `imap_sync` says `except imaplib.IMAP4.abort` and `except imaplib.IMAP4.error`.
    Patching the whole imaplib module turns those into Mock attributes, and
    Python then raises "catching classes that do not inherit from BaseException"
    instead of running the branch - which would pin the mock rather than the
    code. Keeping the real classes on the mocked one makes both clauses mean
    what they mean in production.
    """
    real_error, real_abort = imaplib.IMAP4.error, imaplib.IMAP4.abort
    patcher = mock.patch("helpdesk.email.imaplib.IMAP4")
    mocked_imap4 = patcher.start()
    mocked_imap4.error = real_error
    mocked_imap4.abort = real_abort
    mocked_imap4.return_value = server
    return patcher, mocked_imap4


class MailboxFetchTimeoutTests(TestCase):
    """A socket timeout part way through a fetch must not lose a message.

    `logging_type` is set so `process_email` keeps the queue logger's handlers
    and `assertLogs` can see the failure; with the blank default it clears them
    (`helpdesk/email.py:82-85`).
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(
            title="Timeout",
            slug="timeout",
            allow_email_submission=True,
            email_box_host="0.0.0.1",
            email_box_port="49151",
            logging_type="error",
        )

    def use_transport(self, box_type):
        Queue.objects.filter(pk=self.queue.pk).update(email_box_type=box_type)

    def assert_degraded(self, log_output):
        """The contract every transport shares when a fetch dies mid-run."""
        # The message read before the timeout became a real ticket.
        self.assertEqual(1, Ticket.objects.count())
        self.assertEqual("Fetch me", Ticket.objects.get().title)
        # The failure is logged with its stack trace rather than raised out of
        # the command, so the remaining queues still get their turn.
        self.assertEqual(1, len(log_output))
        self.assertEqual(
            "ERROR:django.helpdesk.queue.timeout:Queue processing failed: "
            "timeout -- timed out",
            log_output[0].splitlines()[0],
        )
        self.assertIn("TimeoutError: timed out", log_output[0])
        # email_box_last_check only advances on success, so the next cron run
        # retries this queue rather than skipping past the unread message.
        self.queue.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertIsNone(self.queue.email_box_last_check)

    def test_a_pop3_timeout_mid_fetch_leaves_the_unread_message_on_the_server(self):
        self.use_transport("pop3")
        server = mock.Mock()
        server.list = mock.Mock(
            return_value=(
                "+OK 2 messages",
                ("1 %d" % len(PLAIN_EMAIL), "2 %d" % len(PLAIN_EMAIL)),
            )
        )

        def retr(number):
            if number == "1":
                return ("+OK", PLAIN_EMAIL.split("\n"))
            raise socket.timeout("timed out")

        server.retr = mock.Mock(side_effect=retr)

        with mock.patch("helpdesk.email.poplib", autospec=True) as mocked_poplib:
            mocked_poplib.POP3 = mock.Mock(return_value=server)
            with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.timeout", "ERROR") as logs:
                call_command("get_email")

        self.assert_degraded(logs.output)
        # Only the message that produced a ticket was deleted from the mailbox.
        self.assertEqual([mock.call("1")], server.dele.call_args_list)
        # Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report: the
        # connection is never closed, because pop3_sync has no try/finally.
        self.assertFalse(server.quit.called)

    def test_an_imap_timeout_mid_fetch_leaves_the_unread_message_on_the_server(self):
        self.use_transport("imap")
        server = mock.Mock()
        server.search = mock.Mock(return_value=("OK", ("1 2",)))

        def fetch(number, _part):
            if number == "1":
                return ("OK", (("1", PLAIN_EMAIL),))
            raise socket.timeout("timed out")

        server.fetch = mock.Mock(side_effect=fetch)
        patcher, _mocked = patched_imap4(server)
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)

        with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.timeout", "ERROR") as logs:
            call_command("get_email")

        self.assert_degraded(logs.output)
        # Only the message that produced a ticket was flagged for deletion.
        self.assertEqual(
            [mock.call("1", "+FLAGS", "\\Deleted")], server.store.call_args_list
        )
        # Pre-existing quirk, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report: expunge,
        # close and logout sit after the try block, so none of them run.
        self.assertFalse(server.logout.called)


class ImapLoginFailureTests(TestCase):
    """A refused IMAP login ends the whole run, not just that queue."""

    def setUp(self):
        for title, slug in (("A broken", "broken"), ("B healthy", "healthy")):
            Queue.objects.create(
                title=title,
                slug=slug,
                allow_email_submission=True,
                email_box_type="imap",
                email_box_host="0.0.0.1",
                email_box_port="49151",
                logging_type="error",
            )

    def test_a_refused_imap_login_stops_every_later_queue(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/email.py:214` calls `sys.exit()` on `IMAP4.abort`. SystemExit
        derives from BaseException, so `process_email`'s `except Exception`
        (`:112`) does not catch it and the loop over queues dies on the spot.
        Queues sorted after the broken one are never polled, and the management
        command exits non-zero. This is what `test_get_email.py`'s
        `test_get_email_with_queue_failure` believes it rules out - that test
        raises a plain Exception, which is caught.
        """
        server = mock.Mock()
        server.login = mock.Mock(side_effect=imaplib.IMAP4.abort("no such user"))
        patcher, mocked_imap4 = patched_imap4(server)
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)

        with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.broken", "ERROR"):
            with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
                call_command("get_email")

        # Only the first queue ever got a connection.
        self.assertEqual(1, mocked_imap4.call_count)
        self.assertFalse(
            Queue.objects.filter(email_box_last_check__isnull=False).exists()
        )


class QueueSchedulingTests(TestCase):
    """`process_email`'s guard for a queue that has never been polled."""

    def test_a_queue_with_file_logging_and_no_previous_check_is_never_polled(self):
        """Pre-existing bug, pinned not fixed - see the unit 7 report.

        `helpdesk/email.py:101` only defaults `email_box_last_check` in the
        branch that has no file handler, so a queue with both `logging_type` and
        `logging_dir` set and a null `email_box_last_check` fails the comparison
        at :104 with a TypeError. It never advances, so it never recovers.
        """
        logging_dir = mkdtemp()
        self.addCleanup(rmtree, logging_dir)
        queue = Queue.objects.create(
            title="Filelog",
            slug="filelog",
            allow_email_submission=True,
            email_box_type="local",
            email_box_local_dir="/var/lib/mail/helpdesk/",
            logging_type="error",
            logging_dir=logging_dir,
        )
        self.assertIsNone(queue.email_box_last_check)

        with mock.patch("os.listdir", return_value=[]):
            with self.assertLogs("django.helpdesk.queue.filelog", "ERROR") as logs:
                call_command("get_email")

        self.assertIn(
            "Queue processing failed: filelog -- unsupported operand type(s) "
            "for +: 'NoneType' and 'datetime.timedelta'",
            logs.output[0],
        )
        queue.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertIsNone(queue.email_box_last_check)

"""Pre-existing behaviour in helpdesk/views/staff.py and update_ticket.py,
pinned rather than fixed.

Unit 10 of the Django 4.2 -> 5.2 migration. Everything here behaves the same
on Django 4.2.30 and 5.2.17 (probed against both installed trees), so none of
it was forced by the migration. Per docs/migration/pattern.md step 6 the
behaviour is asserted as it stands and reported, because a behaviour change
hidden inside a migration diff is invisible to review.

Each test names the bug it pins and points at the report. When one of these is
fixed, the assertion here is what has to be updated.
"""

from base64 import b64encode
from datetime import timedelta
import warnings

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
from django.urls import reverse
from helpdesk.forms import EditTicketCustomFieldForm
from helpdesk.models import (
    CustomField,
    Queue,
    SavedSearch,
    Ticket,
    TicketCustomFieldValue,
)
from helpdesk.update_ticket import update_ticket
from helpdesk.views.staff import calc_basic_ticket_stats


User = get_user_model()


class QuirkTestCase(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Quirk Q", slug="quirk-q")
        self.staff = User.objects.create_user(
            username="quirkstaff", password="pw", email="quirkstaff@example.com"
        )
        self.staff.is_staff = True
        self.staff.save()
        self.client.login(username="quirkstaff", password="pw")


class ReportViewArityTests(QuirkTestCase):
    """``get_report_queryset_or_redirect`` (staff.py:1465) returns a 3-tuple on
    one failure path, a 2-tuple on the other and a 4-tuple on success, but its
    only caller (``run_report``, staff.py:1554) unpacks four values. All three
    failure paths therefore raise ``ValueError`` and the user gets a 500 where
    the code plainly meant to redirect to the report index.
    """

    def test_a_report_with_no_tickets_at_all_raises_instead_of_redirecting(self):
        self.assertEqual(Ticket.objects.count(), 0)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.client.get(
                reverse("helpdesk:run_report", kwargs={"report": "queuemonth"})
            )

    def test_an_unknown_report_name_raises_instead_of_redirecting(self):
        """The url pattern is ``r'^reports/(?P<report>\\w+)/$'``, so any word
        reaches the view and the name check is the only guard."""
        Ticket.objects.create(title="T", queue=self.queue)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.client.get(
                reverse("helpdesk:run_report", kwargs={"report": "not_a_report"})
            )

    def test_a_saved_query_that_will_not_load_raises_instead_of_redirecting(self):
        Ticket.objects.create(title="T", queue=self.queue)
        query = SavedSearch.objects.create(
            title="broken",
            query=b64encode(b"not json at all").decode("ascii"),
            user=self.staff,
        )
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.client.get(
                reverse("helpdesk:run_report", kwargs={"report": "queuemonth"}),
                {"saved_query": query.id},
            )

    def test_a_valid_report_still_renders(self):
        Ticket.objects.create(title="T", queue=self.queue)
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:run_report", kwargs={"report": "queuestatus"})
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.context["title"], "Queue by Status")


class SavedQueryLoadTests(QuirkTestCase):
    """``load_saved_query`` (staff.py:1209) catches ``json.JSONDecodeError``
    only, but ``query_from_base64`` base64-decodes before it parses JSON. A
    saved query whose stored text is not valid base64 raises ``binascii.Error``
    straight out of the handler.
    """

    def test_a_saved_query_that_is_not_base64_escapes_the_handler(self):
        import binascii

        query = SavedSearch.objects.create(
            title="not base64", query="not-base64-at-all", user=self.staff
        )
        with self.assertRaises(binascii.Error):
            self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:list"), {"saved_query": query.id})

    def test_a_saved_query_that_is_base64_but_not_json_redirects_to_the_list(self):
        """The branch the except clause was written for does work."""
        query = SavedSearch.objects.create(
            title="not json",
            query=b64encode(b"not json at all").decode("ascii"),
            user=self.staff,
        )
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:list"), {"saved_query": query.id}
        )
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], reverse("helpdesk:list"))


class CustomFieldsFormTests(QuirkTestCase):
    """Handed over by docs/migration/reports/unit-4.md, section 2.

    ``view_ticket`` (staff.py:472) builds ``EditTicketCustomFieldForm(None,
    instance=ticket)``, which is unbound, so its ``errors`` are always empty on
    the ticket page. The update path builds a second, bound instance in
    ``save_ticket_update`` (staff.py:629) and ``update_ticket.py:321`` saves it
    only ``if customfields_form.is_valid()`` with no ``else``. A custom field
    the user filled in wrongly is therefore dropped in silence.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="Custom field ticket", queue=self.queue, status=Ticket.OPEN_STATUS
        )
        self.field = CustomField.objects.create(
            name="age", label="Age", data_type="integer", required=False
        )

    def test_the_ticket_page_builds_the_custom_fields_form_unbound(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]))
        form = response.context["customfields_form"]
        self.assertFalse(form.is_bound)
        self.assertEqual(dict(form.errors), {})

    def test_an_invalid_custom_field_is_dropped_without_an_error_or_a_change(self):
        customfields_form = EditTicketCustomFieldForm(
            {"custom_age": "not-a-number"}, instance=self.ticket
        )
        self.assertFalse(customfields_form.is_valid())
        self.assertIn("custom_age", customfields_form.errors)

        followup = update_ticket(
            self.staff,
            self.ticket,
            comment="Setting the age",
            customfields_form=customfields_form,
        )

        # The update reports success ...
        self.assertIsNotNone(followup.id)
        # ... but the value never lands ...
        self.assertFalse(
            TicketCustomFieldValue.objects.filter(
                ticket=self.ticket, field=self.field
            ).exists()
        )
        # ... and nothing records that it was thrown away.
        self.assertEqual(
            list(followup.ticketchange_set.values_list("field", flat=True)), []
        )

    def test_a_valid_custom_field_is_saved_and_recorded_as_a_change(self):
        customfields_form = EditTicketCustomFieldForm(
            {"custom_age": "42"}, instance=self.ticket
        )
        self.assertTrue(customfields_form.is_valid())
        followup = update_ticket(
            self.staff,
            self.ticket,
            comment="Setting the age",
            customfields_form=customfields_form,
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            TicketCustomFieldValue.objects.get(
                ticket=self.ticket, field=self.field
            ).value,
            "42",
        )
        self.assertIn(
            "age", followup.ticketchange_set.values_list("field", flat=True)
        )


class AcceptResolutionLinkTests(QuirkTestCase):
    """``view_ticket``'s ``?close`` branch (staff.py:418) calls
    ``update_ticket`` without ``new_status``, so ``update_ticket`` defaults it
    to the ticket's current status. The link labelled "Accepted resolution and
    closed ticket" therefore leaves the ticket resolved, and because
    ``update_ticket.py:349`` assigns ``ticket.resolution = comment`` whenever
    the status is RESOLVED, it also overwrites the resolution with its own
    comment.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="Resolved ticket",
            queue=self.queue,
            status=Ticket.RESOLVED_STATUS,
            resolution="Replaced the widget",
        )

    def test_accepting_a_resolution_does_not_close_the_ticket(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]), {"close": "1"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(response["Location"], self.ticket.get_absolute_url())
        self.ticket.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(self.ticket.status, Ticket.RESOLVED_STATUS)

    def test_accepting_a_resolution_overwrites_the_resolution_with_the_comment(self):
        self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:view", args=[self.ticket.id]), {"close": "1"}
        )
        self.ticket.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(
            self.ticket.resolution, "Accepted resolution and closed ticket"
        )


@override_settings(USE_TZ=True)
class BasicTicketStatsTimezoneTests(QuirkTestCase):
    """``calc_basic_ticket_stats`` (staff.py:1984) is the only place in the
    unit that builds a datetime without ``django.utils.timezone``. It uses
    ``datetime.today()`` and then filters on the ``"%Y-%m-%d"`` string, so
    under timezone support Django parses a naive datetime and warns.

    Django 5.0 flipped the ``USE_TZ`` default from False to True, so an install
    that never set the setting reaches this on upgrade. ``USE_TZ=True`` is
    forced here so both Django versions run the same path.
    """

    def make_ticket(self, title, days_old):
        ticket = Ticket.objects.create(
            title=title, queue=self.queue, status=Ticket.OPEN_STATUS
        )
        from django.utils import timezone

        Ticket.objects.filter(pk=ticket.pk).update(
            created=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=days_old)
        )
        return ticket

    def test_open_tickets_are_bucketed_by_age(self):
        self.make_ticket("fresh", 1)
        self.make_ticket("middle-aged", 45)
        self.make_ticket("ancient", 90)
        stats = calc_basic_ticket_stats(Ticket.objects.all())
        self.assertEqual(
            [(row[0], row[1]) for row in stats["open_ticket_stats"]],
            [
                ("Tickets < 30 days", 1),
                ("Tickets 30 - 60 days", 1),
                ("Tickets > 60 days", 1),
            ],
        )

    def test_the_age_buckets_are_built_from_a_naive_datetime(self):
        """Pinned, not fixed. The warning is Django telling us the 30/60-day
        boundary is the server's local clock read as if it were the project's
        current timezone, so the bucket edges move by the UTC offset."""
        self.make_ticket("ancient", 90)
        with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            warnings.simplefilter("always")
            calc_basic_ticket_stats(Ticket.objects.all())
        naive_warnings = [
            str(w.message)
            for w in caught
            if issubclass(w.category, RuntimeWarning)
            and "naive datetime" in str(w.message)
        ]
        self.assertTrue(naive_warnings, "expected a naive datetime warning")
        self.assertIn("Ticket.created", naive_warnings[0])

    def test_closed_tickets_report_an_average_age_of_zero_when_there_are_none(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            calc_basic_ticket_stats(Ticket.objects.none())[
                "average_nbr_days_until_ticket_closed"
            ],
            0,
        )

"""Contents of the four staff RSS feeds in ``helpdesk/views/feeds.py``.

Added by Unit 6 of the Django 4.2 -> 5.2 migration. ``test_navigation.py`` already
checks that the five ``rss_*`` URLs answer for a staff user and redirect a non-staff
one, but nothing asserted what is inside a feed, and Django 5.2 changed both
``django/contrib/syndication/views.py`` (a new ``stylesheets`` attribute, read through
``_get_dynamic_attr``, which returns ``None`` when a Feed does not define it) and
``django/utils/feedgenerator.py``. These tests pin the selection each feed makes and
the fields it publishes, on both 4.2.30 and 5.2.17.
"""

from datetime import timedelta

from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils import timezone

from helpdesk.models import FollowUp, Queue, Ticket
from helpdesk.tests.helpers import get_staff_user, get_user


class FeedTestCase(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.owner = get_user(username="feed.owner", is_staff=True)
        cls.support = Queue.objects.create(title="Support", slug="support")
        cls.billing = Queue.objects.create(title="Billing", slug="billing")

        cls.open_in_support = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="open in support",
            queue=cls.support,
            description="d",
            status=Ticket.OPEN_STATUS,
            assigned_to=cls.owner,
        )
        cls.reopened_in_billing = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="reopened in billing",
            queue=cls.billing,
            description="d",
            status=Ticket.REOPENED_STATUS,
            assigned_to=cls.owner,
        )
        cls.closed_in_support = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="closed in support",
            queue=cls.support,
            description="d",
            status=Ticket.CLOSED_STATUS,
            assigned_to=cls.owner,
        )
        cls.unassigned_open = Ticket.objects.create(
            title="nobody owns this",
            queue=cls.support,
            description="d",
            status=Ticket.OPEN_STATUS,
        )

    def setUp(self):
        self.viewer = get_staff_user()
        self.client.login(username=self.viewer.get_username(), password="password")

    def feed(self, name, *args):
        response = self.client.get(reverse(name, args=args))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        return response.content.decode()


class OpenTicketsByUserFeedTests(FeedTestCase):
    def test_the_feed_lists_only_open_and_reopened_tickets_for_that_user(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user", self.owner.username)
        self.assertIn("open in support", body)
        self.assertIn("reopened in billing", body)
        self.assertNotIn("closed in support", body)
        self.assertNotIn("nobody owns this", body)

    def test_narrowing_by_queue_drops_the_other_queue(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user_queue", self.owner.username, "support")
        self.assertIn("open in support", body)
        self.assertNotIn("reopened in billing", body)

    def test_the_title_names_the_user_and_the_queue(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user_queue", self.owner.username, "support")
        self.assertIn("Open Tickets in queue Support for feed.owner", body)

    def test_the_link_carries_the_assigned_to_and_queue_filters(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user_queue", self.owner.username, "support")
        self.assertIn(
            "assigned_to=%d&queue=%d" % (self.owner.id, self.support.id), body
        )

    def test_an_unknown_user_is_a_404_rather_than_an_empty_feed(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:rss_user", args=["no.such.user"])
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    def test_an_unknown_queue_is_a_404(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:rss_user_queue", args=[self.owner.username, "nope"])
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    def test_each_item_is_authored_by_the_assignee(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user", self.owner.username)
        self.assertIn("<author>feed.owner</author>", body)


class UnassignedTicketsFeedTests(FeedTestCase):
    def test_only_unassigned_open_tickets_appear(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_unassigned")
        self.assertIn("nobody owns this", body)
        self.assertNotIn("open in support", body)

    def test_an_unassigned_item_is_authored_as_unassigned(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_unassigned")
        self.assertIn("<author>Unassigned</author>", body)


class OpenTicketsByQueueFeedTests(FeedTestCase):
    def test_the_feed_holds_every_open_ticket_in_that_queue(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_queue", "support")
        self.assertIn("open in support", body)
        self.assertIn("nobody owns this", body)
        self.assertNotIn("closed in support", body)
        self.assertNotIn("reopened in billing", body)

    def test_the_title_names_the_queue(self):
        self.assertIn(
            "Open Tickets in queue Support", self.feed("helpdesk:rss_queue", "support")
        )

    def test_an_unknown_queue_slug_is_a_404(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:rss_queue", args=["nope"]))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)


class RecentFollowUpsFeedTests(FeedTestCase):
    def test_followups_are_published_newest_first(self):
        now = timezone.now()
        FollowUp.objects.create(
            ticket=self.open_in_support, title="older note", date=now - timedelta(days=2)
        )
        FollowUp.objects.create(
            ticket=self.open_in_support, title="newer note", date=now - timedelta(days=1)
        )
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_activity")
        self.assertLess(body.index("newer note"), body.index("older note"))

    def test_the_feed_is_capped_at_twenty_items(self):
        now = timezone.now()
        for index in range(25):
            FollowUp.objects.create(
                ticket=self.open_in_support,
                title="note %02d" % index,
                date=now - timedelta(minutes=index),
            )
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_activity")
        self.assertIn("note 00", body)
        self.assertIn("note 19", body)
        self.assertNotIn("note 20", body)

    def test_a_followup_on_a_closed_ticket_still_appears(self):
        # RecentFollowUps has no status filter, unlike the other three feeds.
        FollowUp.objects.create(ticket=self.closed_in_support, title="late reply")
        self.assertIn("late reply", self.feed("helpdesk:rss_activity"))

class OpenTicketsByUserFeedTests(FeedTestCase):
    def test_the_feed_lists_only_open_and_reopened_tickets_for_that_user(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user", self.owner.username)
        self.assertIn("open in support", body)
        self.assertIn("reopened in billing", body)
        self.assertNotIn("closed in support", body)
        self.assertNotIn("nobody owns this", body)

    def test_the_title_names_the_user(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user", self.owner.username)
        self.assertIn("<title>Helpdesk: Open Tickets for feed.owner</title>", body)

    def test_the_link_carries_the_assigned_to_filter(self):
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user", self.owner.username)
        self.assertIn("/tickets/?assigned_to=%d</link>" % self.owner.id, body)

    def test_an_unknown_user_is_a_404_rather_than_an_empty_feed(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:rss_user", args=["no.such.user"])
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    def test_each_item_credits_the_assignee(self):
        # item_author_name with no author email lands in dc:creator, not <author>,
        # in Django's RSS 2.0 generator.
        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user", self.owner.username)
        self.assertIn(">feed.owner</dc:creator>", body)


class OpenTicketsByUserQueueTests(FeedTestCase):
    """The per-queue variant of the user feed.

    The Feed class filters by queue correctly; the URL that is supposed to reach it
    does not exist in practice, so both halves are pinned separately.
    """

    def request(self):
        return self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:rss_user", args=["x"])).wsgi_request

    def test_the_feed_class_narrows_items_to_the_queue(self):
        feed = OpenTicketsByUser()
        obj = feed.get_object(self.request(), self.owner.username, "support")
        self.assertEqual(obj, {"user": self.owner, "queue": self.support})
        self.assertEqual(
            [ticket.title for ticket in feed.items(obj)], ["open in support"]
        )

    def test_the_feed_class_names_the_queue_in_its_title_and_link(self):
        feed = OpenTicketsByUser()
        obj = feed.get_object(self.request(), self.owner.username, "support")
        self.assertEqual(
            feed.title(obj), "Helpdesk: Open Tickets in queue Support for feed.owner"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            feed.link(obj),
            "%s?assigned_to=%d&queue=%d"
            % (reverse("helpdesk:list"), self.owner.id, self.support.id),
        )

    def test_the_queue_url_is_unreachable_and_serves_the_unfiltered_user_feed(self):
        # helpdesk/urls.py:189 registers rss_user as
        # r"^rss/user/(?P<user_name>[^/]+)/" with no "$" anchor, so it matches
        # /rss/user/<name>/<queue>/ first and rss_user_queue (urls.py:194) never
        # resolves. reverse() still builds the two-segment URL, so the link works and
        # quietly returns every queue. helpdesk/urls.py belongs to no unit; reported in
        # docs/migration/reports/unit-6.md rather than fixed here.
        url = reverse("helpdesk:rss_user_queue", args=[self.owner.username, "support"])
        match = resolve(url)
        self.assertEqual(match.url_name, "rss_user")
        self.assertEqual(match.kwargs, {"user_name": self.owner.username})

        body = self.feed("helpdesk:rss_user_queue", self.owner.username, "support")
        self.assertIn("reopened in billing", body)
        self.assertIn("<title>Helpdesk: Open Tickets for feed.owner</title>", body)

    def test_an_unknown_queue_slug_is_therefore_not_a_404(self):
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("helpdesk:rss_user_queue", args=[self.owner.username, "nope"])
        )
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
