# Unit 5 report - public views and knowledge base views

Files owned: `helpdesk/views/public.py`, `helpdesk/views/abstract_views.py`,
`helpdesk/views/kb.py`. Tests owned: `helpdesk/tests/test_public_actions.py`,
`helpdesk/tests/test_ticket_lookup.py`, `helpdesk/tests/test_kb.py`. No new test module
was needed, so the unit's two verification commands are unchanged.

Tests in these three modules go from 10 to 71. Both commands are green:
71 tests OK on Django 5.2.17, 71 tests OK (skipped=3) on 4.2.30. The three skips are the
version-gated LoginRequiredMiddleware assertions described below; each has a non-gated
sibling that asserts the same guarantee on 4.2 through the attribute the middleware reads.

What the migration forced: one change, in two files, and it is the same change both times.
Everything else in this unit is a pre-existing bug pinned by a test rather than fixed, or
something in a file this unit does not own.

## 1. Six public entry points were still exposed to Django 5.1's LoginRequiredMiddleware

**Files:** `helpdesk/views/public.py:43` (`create_ticket`) and `:297`
(`change_language`); `helpdesk/views/kb.py:28` (`index`), `:42` (`category`) and `:77`
(`category_iframe`).

Django 5.1 added `LoginRequiredMiddleware`. It runs in `process_view` and redirects every
anonymous request unless the resolved URL callback carries `login_required = False`. Unit 2
made `protect_view` set that attribute, which covers the five entry points wired through it
(`helpdesk:home`, `my-tickets`, `submit_iframe`, `success_iframe`, `public_view`) and
`helpdesk:login`. It could not cover the rest, because the rest are wired into the URLconf
bare and live in this unit's files:

| URL name | Callback | Was exempt before this unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `helpdesk:submit` | `public.create_ticket` | no |
| `helpdesk:public_change_language` | `public.change_language` | no |
| `helpdesk:kb_index` | `kb.index` | no |
| `helpdesk:kb_category` | `kb.category` | no |
| `helpdesk:kb_category_iframe` | `kb.category_iframe` | no |
| `helpdesk:kb_vote` | `kb.vote` | no, and deliberately still not |

A host project that turns the middleware on therefore loses the public submission form, the
language switcher and the whole knowledgebase to a login redirect, and helpdesk's own
anonymous-access settings (`HELPDESK_ANON_ACCESS_RAISES_404`,
`HELPDESK_REDIRECT_TO_LOGIN_BY_DEFAULT`, `HELPDESK_PUBLIC_VIEW_PROTECTOR`) never get a say,
because the middleware answers first.

The five read-only or policy-bearing views now carry `@login_not_required`, imported from
`helpdesk.decorators` - Unit 2's guarded import, which is Django's decorator on 5.1+ and a
local fallback below that, so the attribute is set identically on 4.2 and the same test
asserts the same guarantee on both. `create_ticket` still runs `protect_view` internally
(`public.py:48`), so the exemption hands the decision back to helpdesk's policy rather than
removing it. `category_iframe` takes the decorator above `xframe_options_exempt` so the
attribute lands on the wrapper the URLconf actually resolves to.

**`kb.vote` is deliberately left without it.** It is the one write in the module, and the
right answer for it is a login, not an exemption; without the attribute,
`LoginRequiredMiddleware` guards it for any project that enables the middleware. See item 5.

Pinned by `PublicViewsOptOutOfBlanketLoginRequirementTests` in `test_public_actions.py` and
`KBOptOutOfBlanketLoginRequirementTests` in `test_kb.py`, each asserting both the attribute
(on 4.2 and 5.2) and, on 5.1+, an anonymous 200 with the middleware actually installed.

## 2. What was checked against the installed 5.2 source and found unchanged

Read in `.venv52/lib/python3.11/site-packages/django/`, and diffed against `.venv`. The
probe that produced most of this ran under both interpreters and its output was diffed; it
is deleted.

| Question | Where it was read | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does `View.as_view()` still copy `dispatch.__dict__` onto the view function, which is the only reason `@csrf_exempt` on a method works? | `views/generic/base.py` | byte-identical file on both |
| Does `CsrfViewMiddleware` still read `csrf_exempt` off the URL callback? | `middleware/csrf.py:419` (4.2) / `:414` (5.2) | same check, same position in the method |
| Did `csrf_exempt` change shape? | `views/decorators/csrf.py:49` / `:51` | rewritten for async in 5.2; still sets `csrf_exempt = True` on the wrapper, still applies `wraps` last, so the flag survives |
| Did `xframe_options_exempt` change shape? | `views/decorators/clickjacking.py` | same rewrite, same `resp.xframe_options_exempt = True` |
| Does `XFrameOptionsMiddleware` still honour that flag? | `middleware/clickjacking.py` | byte-identical on both |
| Did `FormView` / `TemplateView` / `FormMixin` / `ProcessFormView` change? | `views/generic/base.py`, `views/generic/edit.py` | `base.py` identical; `edit.py` only drops the `DeleteView` deprecation shims removed in 5.0, which this unit does not use |
| Did `HttpResponseRedirect` change? | `http/response.py:633` | yes - 5.2 inserts `preserve_request=False` as the **second positional** parameter. Every call in these three files passes exactly one argument, so nothing is affected |
| Did `reverse` change? | `urls/base.py` | 5.2 adds keyword-only `query=` and `fragment=`; purely additive |
| Did `QueryDict` change, for `request.GET.copy()` and `del qparams["kbitem"]`? | `http/request.py` | the class is byte-identical on both |
| Did `render` / `get_object_or_404` change signature? | `shortcuts.py` | no; 5.2 only adds `aget_*` siblings |
| Did `ImproperlyConfigured` / `ObjectDoesNotExist` / `PermissionDenied` change? | `core/exceptions.py` | docstring edits only |

Two settings defaults did change under these views, neither of them a break here:

- **`USE_TZ` flipped from `False` to `True`** (`conf/global_settings.py:44`). `quicktest.py`
  does not set it, so the suite runs naive on 4.2 and aware on 5.2. It shows up in
  `public_view_ticket.html` as a rendered "Submitted On" five hours apart under this
  machine's timezone. `demo/demodesk/config/settings.py:218` and
  `standalone/config/settings.py:220` both already set `USE_TZ = True`, so no shipped
  project is affected; this is a test-harness artefact only. `quicktest.py` is shared and
  edited by nobody, so nothing was done about it. It is worth knowing before anyone writes
  a test in these modules that asserts on a rendered timestamp.
- **`DEFAULT_FILE_STORAGE` is gone** from `global_settings.py`. That is Unit 8's break and
  Unit 8 has landed; no test in this unit uploads an attachment, and none failed on it.

One rendering difference is visible in these views' pages but originates in the form layer:
Django 5.0 adds `aria-describedby` for help text, and 5.2 adds `aria-invalid="true"` plus an
`aria-describedby` pointing at the error, to every widget rendered by
`bootstrap4form`. It is additive and breaks nothing. The redisplay test asserts the
guarantee ("This field is required." reaches the page, the typed body survives) rather than
the markup, so it holds on both versions.

## 3. The iframe views: what the tests now guarantee

`CreateTicketIframeView` and `SuccessIframeView` had two tests between them, neither of
which touched the two exemptions. They now have eleven. The chain being pinned is
non-obvious, which is why it is worth a test rather than a comment: `@csrf_exempt` is
declared on a **method**, `View.as_view()` copies `dispatch.__dict__` onto the view
function, `protect_view`'s `functools.wraps` copies it again onto its own wrapper, and only
then does `CsrfViewMiddleware` see it on the URL callback. Any link in that chain breaking
would silently reintroduce CSRF rejection for every embedded form.

- `test_an_iframe_submission_is_accepted_without_a_csrf_token` posts through a
  `Client(enforce_csrf_checks=True)` and expects the redirect and the saved ticket.
- `test_the_ordinary_public_form_still_rejects_a_post_without_a_csrf_token` posts the same
  payload to `helpdesk:home` and expects 403, so the exemption is proved scoped rather than
  global.
- `test_only_the_iframe_url_entry_carries_the_csrf_exemption_flag` asserts the flag on the
  resolved callback for both URLs, which is the mechanism the two behavioural tests exercise.
- `test_every_iframe_response_may_be_framed` covers all four responses `dispatch` can
  produce - empty form, validation redisplay, redirect after a good submission, success page
  - because the exemption sits on `dispatch` and has to hold for each.
- `test_the_public_homepage_is_not_framable` asserts `X-Frame-Options: DENY` on the
  non-iframe form, as the contrast.

## 4. Pinned pre-existing bugs, not fixed here

All four behave identically on 4.2.30 and 5.2.17, so none of them is migration work. Per
`pattern.md` step 6 they are asserted as they are, with a comment naming the bug, so that a
later fix has to update a test that says what it is changing.

### 4a. A spam submission through the iframe view returns `None` and crashes

**File:** `helpdesk/views/public.py:152-154`.

```python
def form_valid(self, form):
    if super().form_valid(form).status_code == 302:
        return HttpResponseRedirect(reverse("helpdesk:success_iframe"))
```

`BaseCreateTicketView.form_valid` has two exits: a 302 on success and, for a submission
`text_is_spam` flags, `render(request, template_name="helpdesk/public_spam.html")` with
status 200 (`public.py:119-124`). The `if` has no `else`, so on the spam path `form_valid`
returns `None`, `dispatch` returns `None`, and the `xframe_options_exempt` wrapper raises
`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'xframe_options_exempt'`. The same
submission through `helpdesk:home` correctly shows the spam page. Unreachable without an
Akismet key configured (`helpdesk/lib.py:118-126` returns `False` when none is set), which
is why nobody has hit it.

**Intended fix,** for its own commit:

```python
def form_valid(self, form):
    response = super().form_valid(form)
    if response.status_code == 302:
        return HttpResponseRedirect(reverse("helpdesk:success_iframe"))
    return response
```

Pinned by `test_a_spam_submission_through_the_iframe_view_raises`, with
`test_a_spam_submission_through_the_public_form_shows_the_spam_page` next to it as the
working contrast.

### 4b. `?queue=<slug>` on the public form selects nothing

**File:** `helpdesk/views/abstract_views.py:9-13` and `:27-28`.

`AbstractCreateTicketMixin.get_initial` looks the queue up **by slug** and stores its id:

```python
initial_data["queue"] = Queue.objects.get(slug=request.GET.get("queue", None)).id
```

Then `"queue"` is also in `query_param_fields`, and the loop below overwrites that id with
the raw query-string value:

```python
for qpf in query_param_fields:
    initial_data[qpf] = request.GET.get(qpf, initial_data.get(qpf, ""))
```

So the slug reaches a `ChoiceField` whose choices are ids, nothing is preselected, and the
by-slug lookup is dead code. It goes unnoticed because the knowledgebase templates link with
`queue={{category.queue.pk}}` (`templates/helpdesk/kb_category_base.html:40` and `:63`) - an
id, which the loop happens to pass through correctly.

**Intended fix:** drop `"queue"` from `query_param_fields` (the branch above already handles
it), or fall back to the id in the loop. Either changes which queue a `?queue=<slug>` link
preselects, which is a behaviour change and wants its own review.

Pinned by `test_a_queue_slug_in_the_query_string_preselects_nothing`, with
`test_a_queue_id_in_the_query_string_preselects_that_queue` as the working contrast.

### 4c. `/kb/<slug>/?kbitem=abc` is a 500

**File:** `helpdesk/views/kb.py:49-52`.

```python
selected_item = request.GET.get("kbitem", None)
try:
    selected_item = int(selected_item)
except TypeError:
    pass
```

`TypeError` only covers the `None` case. Any non-numeric value raises `ValueError`, which
nobody catches, so a URL anyone can type produces a server error on a fully public page.
`abstract_views.py:41`, three files away, catches `(ValueError, KBItem.DoesNotExist)` for
the same query parameter, which is what the right answer looks like.

**Intended fix:** `except (TypeError, ValueError):`.

Pinned by `test_a_kbitem_parameter_that_is_not_a_number_raises`.

### 4d. Anonymous visitors can vote a knowledgebase item up without limit

**File:** `helpdesk/views/kb.py:83-90`.

`kb.vote` has no authentication decorator, and it identifies the voter by `request.user.pk`,
which is `None` for an anonymous visitor. `item.voted_by.filter(pk=None)` is always empty, so
the "have you already voted" guard never fires; and `item.voted_by.add(None)` writes nothing,
because Django's fast add path issues
`bulk_create(..., ignore_conflicts=True)` (`db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:1521`),
which on SQLite becomes `INSERT OR IGNORE` and silently drops the `NULL` row. The counters
still move. Three anonymous POSTs leave `votes = 3`, `recommendations = 3` and zero recorded
voters, and the same three from a logged-in user leave `votes = 1`.

**Intended fix:** `@login_required` on `kb.vote` (or an early `return
HttpResponseRedirect(item.get_absolute_url())` for an unauthenticated request). Not applied
here for the same reason as the other three: it is not migration work, and it changes what a
public URL does. It is also why `kb.vote` was left out of item 1 - adding
`@login_not_required` there would have written the wrong policy into the code.

Pinned by `test_an_anonymous_vote_moves_the_counters_without_recording_a_voter`, with
`test_a_second_up_vote_from_the_same_user_changes_nothing` as the working contrast.

## 5. Pinned quirk in a file this unit does not own

**File:** `helpdesk/views/public.py:231-232` and `:249-250` - the call sites are this unit's,
but the bug is in how `django.views.generic.View.as_view` is being used and the fix is local,
so it is listed here as a quirk rather than as cross-unit work.

```python
return SearchForTicketView.as_view()(
    request, _("Missing ticket ID or e-mail address. Please try again.")
)
```

The message is passed **positionally**. `View.as_view()`'s inner `view(request, *args,
**kwargs)` puts positional arguments in `self.args`, while
`SearchForTicketView.get_context_data` reads `kwargs.get("error_message", None)` - the URL
keyword arguments, which are always empty for `helpdesk:public_view`. So every "Missing
ticket ID or e-mail address" and "Invalid ticket ID or e-mail address" message is dropped,
and the visitor gets a blank lookup form back with no explanation.
`templates/helpdesk/public_view_form.html:8` has the `{% if error_message %}` block ready for
it.

**Intended fix:** pass it as a keyword - `SearchForTicketView.as_view()(request,
error_message=_("..."))` - which lands it in `self.kwargs` and therefore in
`get_context_data(**kwargs)`. It makes two error messages appear that never appeared before,
which is a visible behaviour change and wants its own commit.

Pinned by `test_a_lookup_missing_the_email_redisplays_the_form_without_its_error`.

## 6. Needs a file this unit does not own

**File:** `helpdesk/tests/helpers.py` - shared by every unit, edited by nobody.

`HAS_LOGIN_REQUIRED_MIDDLEWARE` (`django.VERSION >= (5, 1)`) and
`LOGIN_REQUIRED_MIDDLEWARE` (the dotted path) are now defined three times: in
`test_login.py` (Unit 2), `test_public_actions.py` and `test_kb.py`. The
"install the middleware and issue one request with a fresh `Client`" helper is written twice.
Both belong in `helpdesk/tests/helpers.py` as a constant pair plus a
`get_under_login_required_middleware(url)` function, with the three modules importing them.
Not done here because that file is outside every unit's ownership; it needs whoever
consolidates after all ten units, and it should land together with a rename of Unit 2's
`PUBLIC_VIEW_NAMES` list, which now describes only the `protect_view` half of the public
surface.

## 7. Test coverage added, by module

| Module | Before | After | What the new tests cover |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test_public_actions.py` | 2 | 26 | the iframe submission path end to end, the CSRF exemption and its scope, the validation redisplay, framing on all four iframe responses, both spam branches, `close` on a ticket that is not resolved, the whole of `AbstractCreateTicketMixin`'s query-string seeding, and the two `public.py` login exemptions |
| `test_ticket_lookup.py` | 4 | 19 | the secret-key gate (right, wrong, absent, wrong case, wrong email, unparseable ticket id, ticket that does not exist), and the same lookups with `HELPDESK_VIEW_A_TICKET_PUBLIC` on, where the key is not consulted at all |
| `test_kb.py` | 4 | 26 | a category slug and a KB item that do not exist, a non-public category (404 and absent from the index), a disabled item, the `kbitem` query parameter in all four of its states, framing on the iframe category page, voting (repeat, direction change, GET, anonymous), and the three KB login exemptions |

# Unit 7 report - email ingestion

Files owned: `helpdesk/email.py`, `helpdesk/management/commands/get_email.py`,
`helpdesk/exceptions.py`, `helpdesk/lib.py`. Tests owned:
`helpdesk/tests/test_get_email.py` and the three modules this unit added,
`helpdesk/tests/test_get_email_failures.py`,
`helpdesk/tests/test_get_email_transport.py` and `helpdesk/tests/test_lib.py`.

What the migration forced: one change, `helpdesk/email.py:778-786`. Everything
else in these four files is unchanged in 5.2, and the evidence for that is in
"What was checked against the 5.2 source" below. Everything after that is a
pre-existing bug pinned per pattern step 6 rather than fixed here, or something
in a file this unit does not own, reported per step 7.

## 1. The migration change: `timezone.localtime()` on a naive clock

**File:** `helpdesk/email.py:778-786`, in
`add_file_if_always_save_incoming_email_message`.

Before:

```python
_("original_message.eml").replace(
    ".eml", timezone.localtime().strftime("_%d-%m-%Y_%H:%M") + ".eml"
),
```

`timezone.localtime()` with no argument defaults to `timezone.now()`, and
raises `ValueError: localtime() cannot be applied to a naive datetime` when
that is naive. `now()` is naive whenever `USE_TZ` is off, and **Django 5.0
flipped the `USE_TZ` default from False to True**
(`conf/global_settings.py:44` in both trees, `USE_TZ = False` on 4.2 and
`USE_TZ = True` on 5.2). `quicktest.py` never sets it, so the same code takes a
different branch on each version.

So the direction of the break is the reverse of the usual one: the feature was
broken on Django 4.2's default and the 5.0 default flip hides it. It is still
broken on 5.2 for any project that sets `USE_TZ = False`, which is a supported
setting.

After:

```python
received = timezone.now()
if timezone.is_aware(received):
    received = timezone.localtime(received)
```

with the comment above it saying why. This is the only `timezone.localtime()`
call in the entire library (`grep -rn localtime --include=*.py helpdesk/` has
one other hit, `expects_localtime=True` on a template filter in Unit 1's file),
so there is one boundary to fix and no sibling call sites.

Nothing observable changes on a project with `USE_TZ = True`: `is_aware` is
True, `localtime()` runs exactly as before, and the probe below produces the
identical filename on 4.2 and 5.2 after the change.

**Evidence that the tests catch it.** Reverting the three added lines and
rerunning the new module:

| Django | errors |
| --- | --- |
| 4.2.30 (`USE_TZ` default False) | 4: `test_the_raw_message_is_attached_when_use_tz_is_off`, `test_a_naive_clock_is_stamped_as_is`, `test_an_ingested_message_keeps_a_copy_of_itself_as_an_attachment`, `test_the_colon_in_the_stamped_name_survives_only_in_the_database` |
| 5.2.17 (`USE_TZ` default True) | 2: the two tests that pin `USE_TZ = False` explicitly |

That table is the finding in one line: on 4.2 the whole feature is dead on the
default settings, and on 5.2 only the projects that opt out of `USE_TZ` see it.

**Blast radius:** `HELPDESK_ALWAYS_SAVE_INCOMING_EMAIL_MESSAGE` is a documented
setting (`docs/settings.rst:63` and `:442`) and is off by default, which is why
this survived. It is read at `helpdesk/email.py:777` and nowhere else. No test
in the repo set it before this unit.

## 2. What was checked against the 5.2 source, and found unchanged

Read in `.venv52/lib/python3.11/site-packages/django/`, diffed against the same
file in `.venv/`, never from memory.

| Question | File read | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Did `SimpleUploadedFile` change? | `core/files/uploadedfile.py` | byte-identical 4.2 to 5.2 |
| Did `ValidationError` change? | `core/exceptions.py` | class body identical; the only diff in the file is two docstrings |
| Did `smart_str` / `force_str` change? | `utils/encoding.py` | `DjangoUnicodeDecodeError` dropped its custom `__init__` and now reads `self.object` instead of `self.obj`, and re-raises `from None`. Not reachable here: nothing in `helpdesk/` names that class (grep, no hits), and the only handler, `except UnicodeDecodeError` at `helpdesk/email.py:818`, catches the unchanged base class |
| Is `django.utils.timezone.utc` really gone? | `utils/timezone.py` | yes. 4.2 serves it from a module `__getattr__` with a `RemovedInDjango50Warning`; 5.2 has no `utc` and no pytz support code at all (`_PYTZ_IMPORTED`, `_is_pytz_zone` both gone) |
| Did `timezone.now` / `localtime` change? | `utils/timezone.py:167-203` | byte-identical bodies |
| Did `BaseCommand` change? | `core/management/base.py` | yes, three ways, none reachable from `get_email.py`: `OutputWrapper` is now registered as a virtual `TextIOBase` rather than subclassing it, `check` gained a `get_check_kwargs` hook, and `CommandParser` sets `color=False` on Python 3.14. `get_email.py` only defines `help`, `add_arguments` and `handle` |
| Did `Q` composition change? | `db/models/query_utils.py` | additive only (`replace_expressions` added). `Q(queues=q) | Q(queues__isnull=True)` at `email.py:1085` is unaffected |
| Did `request.headers` change? | `http/request.py` | `HttpHeaders` differs by one line, `header[len(prefix):]` became `header.removeprefix(prefix)`. Same semantics; used at `helpdesk/lib.py:140-141` |

**pytz.** Nothing in `helpdesk/` imports pytz or names `timezone.utc`:
`grep -rn -e pytz -e 'timezone\.utc' --include="*.py" helpdesk/ quicktest.py`
returns one hit, `helpdesk/views/staff.py:166`, which is the GET parameter
`utcr_page` and not a timezone at all. pytz 2026.3 is installed in both venvs as
a transitive dependency but is imported by neither the library nor its tests.

**The probe.** A script importing these four modules and printing the output of
26 calls (encoding edges, undecodable payloads, bogus charsets, hostile upload
names, malformed MIME, subject decoding) was run under both venvs and the
outputs diffed. After the fix in section 1 the diff is five lines, and all five
are facts about Django itself rather than helpdesk behaviour: the version
string, `settings.USE_TZ`, the tzinfo on `now()`, whether bare `localtime()`
works, and whether `django.utils.timezone.utc` exists. Every helpdesk function
in the probe returns the identical value on both versions. The probe lived
outside the repo and is deleted.

## 3. Failure injection added

`test_get_email.py` had 28 test methods (43 executed, since
`GetEmailParametricTemplate` is instantiated once per mailbox type) and not one
of them hands the ingester something broken. None of its 43 were modified. 24
were added across three new modules. Every pinned behaviour below was confirmed
identical on 4.2.30 and 5.2.17 before being written down.

**`helpdesk/tests/test_get_email_failures.py`** - message-level failures.

- The `.eml` copy of the incoming message is attached with `USE_TZ` off, with
  it on, and end to end under whichever default the running Django has. Two
  tests freeze the clock at 23:30 UTC inside a UTC+05:30 zone and pin that the
  stamped name is local wall clock (`_06-03-2024_05:00`), not UTC, in both
  configurations. This is the section 1 coverage.
- A multipart whose declared boundary never appears: the message is **not**
  dropped, it files a ticket whose `description` is `None` and whose followup
  comment is `""`.
- A `multipart/related` holding only an image: `AttributeError`, no ticket. See
  section 4.1.
- An attachment with an unregistered media type: named `part-1None`. See
  section 4.2.
- Four attachment filenames the filesystem will not take verbatim:
  `../../etc/passwd` (reduced to `passwd`, provably inside the ticket's
  attachment directory), `../` (aborts the queue, section 4.3), a NUL byte
  (section 4.4) and a 300-character name (truncated to 255, extension kept).

**`helpdesk/tests/test_get_email_transport.py`** - mailbox-connection failures.
No real socket is opened; the servers are Mocks whose second call raises.

- POP3 and IMAP socket timeout part way through a fetch. Both assert the same
  four-part contract: the message read before the timeout became a real ticket,
  only that message was deleted or flagged on the server, the failure was logged
  with its stack trace rather than raised out of the command, and
  `email_box_last_check` was **not** advanced, so the next cron run retries.
  Nothing is silently dropped. Each then pins the leak in section 4.5.
- A refused IMAP login: `SystemExit`, and the second queue never gets a
  connection. See section 4.6.
- A queue with file logging configured and no previous check: never polled, ever.
  See section 4.7.

**`helpdesk/tests/test_lib.py`** - `lib.py` had no test module at all.
`process_attachments` was reached sideways from `test_attachments.py` and
`text_is_spam` by nothing. Six tests: the spam check is dead (section 4.8), a
zero-byte attachment is dropped silently (section 4.9), a file over
`HELPDESK_MAX_EMAIL_ATTACHMENT_SIZE` is saved but not returned for mailing, a
rejected extension raises only after the valid files are committed, and two
files rejected for the same reason collapse into one error.

The IMAP tests patch `helpdesk.email.imaplib.IMAP4` alone and put the real
`IMAP4.error` and `IMAP4.abort` classes back onto the mock. Patching the whole
`imaplib` module - which is what `test_get_email.py` does - turns
`except imaplib.IMAP4.error` at `email.py:262` into a Mock attribute, and Python
raises `TypeError: catching classes that do not inherit from BaseException`
instead of running the branch. Any test written the other way pins the mock, not
the code.

## 4. Pre-existing bugs and quirks, pinned rather than fixed

All nine behave identically on 4.2.30 and 5.2.17, so nothing about the migration
forced them and a behaviour change hidden inside a migration diff is invisible
to review. Each is pinned by a test that names it and points here.

### 4.1 A `multipart/related` with no text part crashes the queue

`helpdesk/email.py:899`, in `extract_email_message_content`:

```python
if "multipart/related" == content_type:
    parent_part = message_part
    message_part = message_part.get_body(preferencelist=["html", "plain"])
    content_type = message_part.get_content_type()   # message_part can be None
```

The first `get_body()` at `:884` is guarded (`if not message_part: return None,
None` at `:885`); the second is not. A `multipart/related` carrying only an
image - which real clients send - raises `AttributeError`. Only `TypeError` is
caught in `imap_sync` (`:245`) and `imap_oauth_sync` (`:345`), and `pop3_sync`
and the local-directory path catch nothing, so it reaches `process_email`'s
`except Exception` at `:112`: the queue aborts, every later message in it is
left unread, and `email_box_last_check` is not advanced. One malformed message
stops that queue on every run until it is removed by hand.

**Intended fix,** for its own commit: give the second `get_body()` the same
guard as the first, falling back to the related part itself when there is no
html or plain alternative, so the image is processed as an attachment and the
ticket gets an empty body - which is what
`test_with_attachment_but_no_body_part` already proves the rest of the pipeline
handles.

**Pinned by** `test_a_related_part_with_no_text_alternative_aborts_the_whole_queue`.

### 4.2 An unregistered media type produces the literal filename suffix "None"

`helpdesk/email.py:961`, in `process_as_attachment`:

```python
ext = mimetypes.guess_extension(part.get_content_type())
name = f"part-{counter}{ext}"
```

`guess_extension` returns `None` for a type it does not know, and the f-string
stringifies it, so the attachment is stored as `part-1None`. Cosmetic, but it
also means `mimetypes.guess_type(name)` on the next line returns `None` and the
row falls back to `application/octet-stream`.

**Intended fix:** `name = f"part-{counter}{ext or ''}"`.

**Pinned by** `test_an_attachment_with_an_unregistered_media_type_is_named_part_1none`.

### 4.3 A filename that is only a traversal aborts the queue

`helpdesk/email.py:967` passes the assembled name straight to
`SimpleUploadedFile`. Django's `UploadedFile.name` setter runs
`validate_file_name` and then `os.path.basename`. For `filename="../"` the
basename is empty, so Django raises
`SuspiciousFileOperation: Could not derive file name from ''` and
`process_as_attachment` lets it out. Same blast radius as 4.1: the whole queue
aborts over one attachment.

This is Django's traversal defence working as designed - `../../etc/passwd`
lands as `passwd` inside the ticket's own directory, which
`test_a_traversing_filename_cannot_escape_the_ticket_directory` proves. The bug
is only that `process_as_attachment` has no handler for the case where the
defence leaves nothing behind. Worth noting that the same defence silently
discards the `part-N_` prefix, so two traversing attachments on one message
collide on name.

**Intended fix:** wrap the `files.append` in
`try/except SuspiciousFileOperation`, log the rejected name and carry on to the
next part, matching how a rejected extension is already handled at
`email.py:684-685`.

**Pinned by** `test_a_filename_that_is_only_a_traversal_aborts_the_whole_queue`.

### 4.4 A NUL byte in a filename leaves the row and the file disagreeing

Django's storage runs `get_valid_filename`, which strips the NUL, so the file
lands as `part-1_ab.txt`. `helpdesk/lib.py:162` writes the unsanitised
`smart_str(attached.name)` to the `filename` column, so the row says
`part-1_a\x00b.txt`. The two disagree, and on PostgreSQL the row write raises
`ValueError: A string literal cannot contain NUL (0x00) characters` - which
would abort the queue the way 4.1 and 4.3 do. The test suite runs on SQLite, so
it can only pin the mismatch, not the Postgres failure.

**Intended fix:** derive the `filename` column from the name the storage
actually used, or run `get_valid_filename` before building the model instance.
That is `helpdesk/lib.py`, this unit's file, but it changes the stored name for
every attachment path in the project - forms, the update view and email all go
through `process_attachments` - so it needs its own commit and its own review.

**Pinned by**
`test_a_nul_byte_in_a_filename_is_stripped_on_disk_but_kept_in_the_row`.

### 4.5 A dead connection is never closed

`pop3_sync` (`helpdesk/email.py:134-192`) calls `server.quit()` as the last
statement of the function, and `imap_sync` calls `expunge` / `close` / `logout`
at `:268-270`, all outside any `finally`. Any exception from a fetch skips them,
so the socket is left to the garbage collector. Harmless on a cron run that
exits, a slow leak in a long-lived process.

**Intended fix:** a `try/finally` around each sync body.

**Pinned by** the two timeout tests' closing assertions.

### 4.6 A refused IMAP login ends the whole run, not just that queue

`helpdesk/email.py:214` (and `:310` in `imap_oauth_sync`) calls `sys.exit()`
after logging an IMAP `abort`. `SystemExit` derives from `BaseException`, so
`process_email`'s `except Exception` at `:112` does not catch it. The loop over
queues dies where it stands: every queue sorted after the broken one is never
polled, and the management command exits non-zero.

This is what `test_get_email.py`'s `test_get_email_with_queue_failure` believes
it rules out. That test raises a plain `Exception` from a mocked
`process_queue`, which is caught, so it passes while the real failure mode is
not covered.

**Intended fix:** raise a `CommandError` (or just let the exception propagate to
the existing handler) instead of `sys.exit()`, so one unreachable mailbox costs
one queue rather than the run. Three call sites, all in `email.py`.

**Pinned by** `test_a_refused_imap_login_stops_every_later_queue`.

### 4.7 A queue with file logging and no previous check is never polled

`helpdesk/email.py:91-104`:

```python
if (q.logging_type in logging_types) and q.logging_dir:
    log_file_handler = logging.FileHandler(...)
    logger.addHandler(log_file_handler)
else:
    log_file_handler = None
    if not q.email_box_last_check:
        q.email_box_last_check = timezone.now() - timedelta(minutes=30)
try:
    queue_time_delta = timedelta(minutes=q.email_box_interval or 0)
    if (q.email_box_last_check + queue_time_delta) < timezone.now():
```

The default for a null `email_box_last_check` only exists in the branch that has
no file handler. A queue configured with both `logging_type` and `logging_dir` -
the documented way to get per-queue log files - and never yet polled therefore
fails `:104` with
`TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'datetime.timedelta'`.
`email_box_last_check` is only written after a successful `process_queue`, so it
stays null and the queue fails identically forever. The only way out is to set
the column by hand.

**Intended fix:** hoist the `if not q.email_box_last_check:` default above the
`if/else`, where it belongs - it has nothing to do with logging.

**Pinned by** `test_a_queue_with_file_logging_and_no_previous_check_is_never_polled`.

### 4.8 Spam checking is silently off on every install

`helpdesk/lib.py:102-105`:

```python
try:
    from akismet import Akismet
except ImportError:
    return False
```

akismet 2.0 removed the `Akismet` class in favour of `SyncClient` / `AsyncClient`
plus a `Config`. The version installed in both venvs is 25.10.1, which exports
`SyncClient`, `AsyncClient`, `Config` and no `Akismet` at all, so this import
raises `ImportError` and `text_is_spam` returns `False` unconditionally. Every
public ticket submission is waved through (`helpdesk/views/public.py:117`, Unit
5's file, is the only caller).

The `except ImportError` was written to mean "akismet is not installed". It now
also swallows "akismet is installed but its API moved", and the caller cannot
tell a passing spam check from one that never ran. `requirements.txt:5` pins
`akismet` with no version at all.

**Intended fix,** and it needs two files: rewrite `text_is_spam` against
`akismet.SyncClient` / `Config` (this unit's file) and give `requirements.txt` a
floor that matches (**Unit 3's file** - the exact pin depends on which API is
chosen, `>=24.5.0` is the first release with `SyncClient`). Narrowing the
`except` so an installed-but-incompatible akismet is loud rather than silent is
the part that matters.

**Pinned by** `test_the_installed_akismet_no_longer_exposes_the_class_lib_imports`,
which asserts the cause, and
`test_spam_checking_is_off_and_the_import_failure_is_swallowed`, which asserts
the effect. The first fails loudly if the dependency floor ever moves back.

### 4.9 A zero-byte attachment is dropped without a word

`helpdesk/lib.py:159` wraps the whole loop body in `if attached.size:`, so an
empty upload is neither saved nor added to the error set. `process_attachments`
returns normally and the submitter is told the upload succeeded.

**Intended fix:** either save it or add a `ValidationError` for it, but not
nothing. Same file and same commit as 4.4.

**Pinned by** `test_a_zero_byte_attachment_is_dropped_without_a_word`.

### 4.10 The stamped `.eml` name carries a colon

`helpdesk/email.py:793` formats the timestamp as `_%d-%m-%Y_%H:%M`. Django's
storage strips the colon via `get_valid_filename`, so the `filename` column and
the file on disk disagree - the same class of mismatch as 4.4, and the name is
not portable to a filesystem that rejects colons. Changing the format would
rename the file for every existing install, so it is pinned, not changed, even
though the line is in this unit's file and this unit touched the statement above
it.

**Pinned by** `test_the_colon_in_the_stamped_name_survives_only_in_the_database`.

## 5. Needing a file this unit does not own

- **`requirements.txt:5`** (Unit 3): `akismet` is pinned with no version, which
  is how 4.8 happened. Whatever floor is chosen has to match the API
  `helpdesk/lib.py` is rewritten against.
- **`helpdesk/tests/test_get_email.py`** is this unit's own module and was not
  modified; `test_get_email_with_queue_failure` is misleading rather than wrong
  (see 4.6), and the honest fix is to add the `SystemExit` case, which this unit
  did in a new module instead of editing an existing assertion.

Nothing else was needed. `helpdesk/models.py` was read but not touched: Unit 8's
`ensure_attachment_directory` and the `default_storage` check at
`models.py:1189-1210` were already in place, so every attachment test here ran
green on 5.2 without a `DEFAULT_FILE_STORAGE` shim.

"""How ``helpdesk/webhooks.py`` behaves when the far end misbehaves.

Added by Unit 6 of the Django 4.2 -> 5.2 migration. ``test_webhooks.py`` covers the
happy path against a real local HTTP server; nothing covered what happens when a
webhook endpoint is slow, down, or answers with an error, and both senders run inside
the request that created the ticket, so the answer decides whether a broken webhook
takes ticket creation down with it.

The behaviour pinned here is unchanged between Django 4.2.30 and 5.2.17. Two of these
tests pin a gap rather than a guarantee; they say so, and
``docs/migration/reports/unit-6.md`` carries the detail.
"""

from unittest import mock

import requests

from django.test import TestCase

from helpdesk import settings as helpdesk_settings
from helpdesk import webhooks
from helpdesk.models import FollowUp, Queue, Ticket


class WebhookDeliveryTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.queue = Queue.objects.create(title="Hooked", slug="hooked")
        cls.ticket = Ticket.objects.create(
            queue=cls.queue, title="Hook me", description="d"
        )
        cls.followup = FollowUp.objects.create(ticket=cls.ticket, title="note")

    def urls(self, new_ticket=None, followup=None):
        return mock.patch.multiple(
            helpdesk_settings,
            HELPDESK_GET_NEW_TICKET_WEBHOOK_URLS=lambda: new_ticket,
            HELPDESK_GET_FOLLOWUP_WEBHOOK_URLS=lambda: followup,
        )

    def test_no_configured_url_means_no_request_is_made(self):
        with self.urls(), mock.patch.object(webhooks.requests, "post") as post:
            webhooks.send_new_ticket_webhook(self.ticket)
            webhooks.notify_followup_webhooks(self.followup)
        post.assert_not_called()

    def test_every_configured_url_receives_the_new_ticket_payload(self):
        targets = ["http://one.example.com/hook", "http://two.example.com/hook"]
        with self.urls(new_ticket=targets), mock.patch.object(
            webhooks.requests, "post"
        ) as post:
            webhooks.send_new_ticket_webhook(self.ticket)

        self.assertEqual([call.args[0] for call in post.call_args_list], targets)
        payload = post.call_args_list[0].kwargs["json"]
        self.assertEqual(payload["queue_slug"], "hooked")
        self.assertEqual(payload["ticket"]["id"], self.ticket.id)
        self.assertEqual(payload["ticket"]["title"], "Hook me")
        self.assertNotIn("followup_id", payload)

    def test_the_followup_payload_names_the_followup_and_its_ticket(self):
        with self.urls(followup=["http://one.example.com/hook"]), mock.patch.object(
            webhooks.requests, "post"
        ) as post:
            webhooks.notify_followup_webhooks(self.followup)

        payload = post.call_args.kwargs["json"]
        self.assertEqual(payload["followup_id"], self.followup.id)
        self.assertEqual(payload["queue_slug"], "hooked")
        self.assertEqual(payload["ticket"]["id"], self.ticket.id)

    def test_the_configured_timeout_is_passed_to_every_call(self):
        with self.urls(new_ticket=["http://one.example.com/hook"]), mock.patch.object(
            webhooks.requests, "post"
        ) as post:
            webhooks.send_new_ticket_webhook(self.ticket)
        self.assertEqual(
            post.call_args.kwargs["timeout"],
            helpdesk_settings.HELPDESK_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT,
        )

    def test_a_timeout_is_logged_and_does_not_reach_the_caller(self):
        targets = ["http://slow.example.com/hook", "http://fine.example.com/hook"]
        with self.urls(new_ticket=targets), mock.patch.object(
            webhooks.requests, "post", side_effect=requests.exceptions.Timeout
        ) as post:
            with self.assertLogs("helpdesk.webhooks", level="ERROR") as logs:
                webhooks.send_new_ticket_webhook(self.ticket)
        # Both targets are still attempted: the loop swallows per URL, not per batch.
        self.assertEqual(post.call_count, 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(logs.output), 2)

    def test_a_refused_connection_propagates_to_the_caller(self):
        # Gap, not a guarantee: webhooks.py catches Timeout only, so a webhook host
        # that is down turns ticket creation into a 500 for the submitter. Pinned as
        # it is; changing it is a behaviour change, not a migration fix.
        with self.urls(new_ticket=["http://down.example.com/hook"]), mock.patch.object(
            webhooks.requests,
            "post",
            side_effect=requests.exceptions.ConnectionError,
        ):
            with self.assertRaises(requests.exceptions.ConnectionError):
                webhooks.send_new_ticket_webhook(self.ticket)

    def test_an_error_status_from_the_endpoint_is_ignored(self):
        # Gap, not a guarantee: nothing calls raise_for_status, so a 500 from the
        # receiver is indistinguishable from success and the delivery is not retried.
        response = mock.Mock(status_code=500)
        with self.urls(new_ticket=["http://broken.example.com/hook"]), mock.patch.object(
            webhooks.requests, "post", return_value=response
        ) as post:
            webhooks.send_new_ticket_webhook(self.ticket)
        self.assertEqual(post.call_count, 1)

    def test_the_serialized_ticket_carries_its_custom_field_values(self):
        # send_new_ticket_webhook calls set_custom_field_values before serializing,
        # which is the only reason custom_* keys appear in the payload.
        from helpdesk.models import CustomField

        CustomField.objects.create(
            name="team", label="Team", data_type="varchar", max_length=20
        )
        self.ticket.save_custom_field_values({"custom_team": "core"})
        with self.urls(new_ticket=["http://one.example.com/hook"]), mock.patch.object(
            webhooks.requests, "post"
        ) as post:
            webhooks.send_new_ticket_webhook(self.ticket)
        self.assertEqual(post.call_args.kwargs["json"]["ticket"]["custom_team"], "core")

        """5.2 rebuilt ``redirect_to_login`` on ``urlsplit``/``urlunsplit``,
        which index the query differently from ``urlparse``. The value that
        comes back still has to be the whole original URL, query included."""
        url = reverse("helpdesk:list")

        location = urlsplit(response["Location"])
        self.assertEqual(location.path, reverse("helpdesk:login"))

126	## 4. New coverage
127	
128	`helpdesk/tests/test_custom_field_forms.py`, 32 tests:
129	
130	- **Construction.** That `CustomField.DATA_TYPE_CHOICES` and the form's mapping still
131	  cover the same thirteen types (a type the form cannot build raises `NameError` at
132	  request time); the field class each type builds; the widget class and CSS class each
133	  gets, which is a contract with `helpdesk/js/init_datetime_classes.js` selecting on
134	  `.date-field`, `.datetime-field` and `.time-field`; label, help_text, required and
135	  max_length coming off the row; decimal precision; list options and the optional
136	  empty first choice; the url scheme; and the `NameError` branch naming the bad type.
137	- **Round trip.** One test per data type: posted through `PublicTicketForm`, saved,
138	  the stored `TicketCustomFieldValue.value` asserted, and the value read back as
139	  `EditTicketForm`'s initial. That covers both directions of the date/time/boolean
140	  string conversions, which live in two different modules
141	  (`convert_value` out, `EditTicketForm.__init__` back in). Plus a second save
142	  updating the existing row rather than adding one.
143	- **Rejection.** A required custom field left empty; the same error asserted as a
144	  field error with a resolvable label id rather than a form error; an integer given
145	  a word; a list option that is not offered; a varchar over its max_length. Each
146	  asserts no `Ticket` and no `TicketCustomFieldValue` was written. Plus the
147	  staff_only filter in both directions.
148	
149	`helpdesk/tests/test_form_validators.py`, 31 tests: the `validate_file_extension`
150	accept and reject matrix including case, the no-extension and bare-dot exits, the
151	last-suffix-only rule, the allow list being read at call time and validation being
152	switched off; the public attachment field carrying the validator, rejecting `.exe`
153	through the form and through a real POST to `helpdesk:home`, and accepting `.txt` all
154	the way to a `FollowUpAttachment`; form media order and merging; the checklist forms;
155	and `MultipleTicketSelectForm.clean_tickets`, whose three rejection branches (fewer
156	than two, more than four, mixed queues) had no test - `test_ticket_actions` covers
157	only the happy path through the view.
158	
159	## 5. Pinned, not fixed
160	
161	Per pattern step 6. All three behave identically on 4.2 and 5.2, so none of them is a
162	migration change, and each is asserted as it stands with a comment saying so.
163	
164	1. **`clean_task_list` trusts the shape of the JSON it is given.**
165	   `helpdesk/forms.py:768-770`:
166	
167	   ```python
168	   def clean_task_list(self):
169	       task_list = self.cleaned_data["task_list"]
170	       return list(map(lambda task: task.strip(), task_list))
171	   ```
172	
173	   `task_list` is a `JSONField`, so it accepts any JSON value. A JSON string is
174	   iterable, so `"abc"` cleans to `["a", "b", "c"]`. A JSON number is not iterable, so
175	   `42` raises `TypeError` out of `clean_task_list` - not a `ValidationError`, so it
176	   escapes the form and becomes a 500 on `helpdesk:checklist_templates` rather than a
177	   field error. The hidden input is written by the page's own JS, so only a hand-made
178	   POST gets there. Pinned by `test_a_json_string_task_list_is_split_into_characters`
179	   and `test_a_numeric_task_list_raises_out_of_clean`.
180	
181	   Intended fix, for its own commit: validate the shape first, raising
182	   `ValidationError(_("Enter a list of tasks."))` when the decoded value is not a list
183	   of strings, then strip. That turns a 500 into a field error and changes what a
184	   string payload does, so it needs review a migration diff would not get.
185	
186	2. **`EditTicketCustomFieldForm.save()` returns `None`.** `helpdesk/forms.py:248`
187	   calls `super().save(*args, **kwargs)` without returning it, so it breaks the
188	   `ModelForm.save()` contract of handing back the instance. Harmless today: the only
189	   caller is `helpdesk/update_ticket.py:322`, which discards the result. Left unpinned
190	   deliberately - no test should depend on a broken contract that nothing reads, and
191	   adding `return` needs no test change when someone does it.
192	
193	3. **`validate_file_extension` splits the filename before checking whether validation
194	   is switched off.** `helpdesk/validators.py:18` runs `os.path.splitext(value.name)`
195	   above the `HELPDESK_VALIDATE_ATTACHMENT_TYPES` early return at `:22`, so a value
196	   with no `.name` raises `AttributeError` even when the check is disabled. No caller
197	   passes anything but an `UploadedFile`. Not pinned by a test; moving two lines is
198	   obvious enough to do in a cleanup commit.
199	
200	The extension check itself is name-based and inspects only the last suffix, so
201	`malware.exe.txt` is accepted and `notes.tar.gz` is rejected. That is the documented
202	intent of the TODO at `helpdesk/validators.py:19`, not a regression, and it is pinned
203	by `test_only_the_last_suffix_is_inspected` so that a future content-sniffing fix has
204	to say so.
205	
206	## 6. Needs a file this unit does not own
207	
208	1. **`quicktest.py` does not set `USE_TZ`** (shared file, no unit owns it). The
209	   consequence is in section 3: the 4.2 baseline runs with timezone support off and
210	   the 5.2 run has it on, so the two verification commands are not running the same
211	   configuration. Nothing fails today. Whoever integrates the ten units should decide
212	   whether the suite pins `USE_TZ=True` explicitly - which is what
213	   `demo/demodesk/config/settings.py` and `standalone/config/settings.py` already do,
214	   so it would match a real install - and rerun the whole suite on 4.2 with it set.
215	
216	2. **`helpdesk/tests/test_checklist.py:170` writes a naive datetime.**
217	   `completion_date=datetime(2023, 5, 1)` is naive, so on 5.2 the save emits
218	   `RuntimeWarning: DateTimeField ChecklistTask.completion_date received a naive
219	   datetime (2023-05-01 00:00:00) while time zone support is active.` and Django
220	   interprets it in the default timezone. The test still passes, and this unit may not
221	   edit existing test code, so it is left alone. The edit I would make:
222	
223	   ```python
224	   task = checklist.tasks.create(
225	       description="Task", position=1, completion_date=timezone.now()
226	   )
227	   ```
228	
229	   with `from django.utils import timezone`. The test only asserts the field is not
230	   `None` before and `None` after, so the exact instant does not matter, and
231	   `timezone.now()` is naive on 4.2 and aware on 5.2 - correct under either setting.
232	   `timezone.make_aware(...)` would not be: an aware value with `USE_TZ` off makes the
233	   sqlite backend raise.
234	
235	3. **`helpdesk/models.py:2069`, `CustomField._choices_as_array`** (Unit 8) returns a
236	   list of two-item lists. Django 5.2 normalises those to 2-tuples inside
237	   `ChoiceField`, so nothing breaks and no change is needed. Noted only so that Unit 8
238	   knows the shape crosses a normalising boundary now.
239	
240	4. **`helpdesk/settings.py:260-269`, `CUSTOMFIELD_TO_FIELD_DICT`** (shared file). The
241	   url entry is what section 1 is about; the fix went into `forms.py` because that is
242	   where the class is instantiated and because this unit does not own settings.
243	   Nothing in the dict needs to change.

159	raises `TypeError: catching classes that do not inherit from BaseException`
160	instead of running the branch. Any test written the other way pins the mock, not
161	the code.
162	
163	## 4. Pre-existing bugs and quirks, pinned rather than fixed
164	
165	All nine behave identically on 4.2.30 and 5.2.17, so nothing about the migration
166	forced them and a behaviour change hidden inside a migration diff is invisible
167	to review. Each is pinned by a test that names it and points here.
168	
169	### 4.1 A `multipart/related` with no text part crashes the queue
170	
171	`helpdesk/email.py:899`, in `extract_email_message_content`:
172	
173	```python
174	if "multipart/related" == content_type:
175	    parent_part = message_part
176	    message_part = message_part.get_body(preferencelist=["html", "plain"])
177	    content_type = message_part.get_content_type()   # message_part can be None
178	```
179	
180	The first `get_body()` at `:883` is guarded (`if not message_part: return None,
181	None` at `:885`); the second, at `:893`, is not. A `multipart/related` carrying only an
182	image - which real clients send - raises `AttributeError`. Only `TypeError` is
183	caught in `imap_sync` (`:245`) and `imap_oauth_sync` (`:345`), and `pop3_sync`
184	and the local-directory path catch nothing, so it reaches `process_email`'s
185	`except Exception` at `:112`: the queue aborts, every later message in it is
186	left unread, and `email_box_last_check` is not advanced. One malformed message
187	stops that queue on every run until it is removed by hand.
188	
189	**Intended fix,** for its own commit: give the second `get_body()` the same
190	guard as the first, falling back to the related part itself when there is no
191	html or plain alternative, so the image is processed as an attachment and the
192	ticket gets an empty body - which is what
193	`test_with_attachment_but_no_body_part` already proves the rest of the pipeline
194	handles.
195	
196	**Pinned by** `test_a_related_part_with_no_text_alternative_aborts_the_whole_queue`.
197	
198	### 4.2 An unregistered media type produces the literal filename suffix "None"
199	
200	`helpdesk/email.py:961`, in `process_as_attachment`:
201	
202	```python
203	ext = mimetypes.guess_extension(part.get_content_type())
204	name = f"part-{counter}{ext}"
205	```
206	
207	`guess_extension` returns `None` for a type it does not know, and the f-string
208	stringifies it, so the attachment is stored as `part-1None`. Cosmetic, but it
209	also means `mimetypes.guess_type(name)` on the next line returns `None` and the
210	row falls back to `application/octet-stream`.
211	
212	**Intended fix:** `name = f"part-{counter}{ext or ''}"`.
213	
214	**Pinned by** `test_an_attachment_with_an_unregistered_media_type_is_named_part_1none`.
215	
216	### 4.3 A filename that is only a traversal aborts the queue
217	
218	`helpdesk/email.py:967` passes the assembled name straight to
219	`SimpleUploadedFile`. Django's `UploadedFile.name` setter runs
220	`validate_file_name` and then `os.path.basename`. For `filename="../"` the
221	basename is empty, so Django raises
222	`SuspiciousFileOperation: Could not derive file name from ''` and
223	`process_as_attachment` lets it out. Same blast radius as 4.1: the whole queue
224	aborts over one attachment.
225	
226	This is Django's traversal defence working as designed - `../../etc/passwd`
227	lands as `passwd` inside the ticket's own directory, which
228	`test_a_traversing_filename_cannot_escape_the_ticket_directory` proves. The bug
229	is only that `process_as_attachment` has no handler for the case where the
230	defence leaves nothing behind. Worth noting that the same defence silently
231	discards the `part-N_` prefix, so two traversing attachments on one message
232	collide on name.
233	
234	**Intended fix:** wrap the `files.append` in
235	`try/except SuspiciousFileOperation`, log the rejected name and carry on to the
236	next part, matching how a rejected extension is already handled at
237	`email.py:684-685`.
238	
239	**Pinned by** `test_a_filename_that_is_only_a_traversal_aborts_the_whole_queue`.
240	
241	### 4.4 A NUL byte in a filename leaves the row and the file disagreeing
242	
243	Django's storage runs `get_valid_filename`, which strips the NUL, so the file
244	lands as `part-1_ab.txt`. `helpdesk/lib.py:162` writes the unsanitised
245	`smart_str(attached.name)` to the `filename` column, so the row says
246	`part-1_a\x00b.txt`. The two disagree, and on PostgreSQL the row write raises
247	`ValueError: A string literal cannot contain NUL (0x00) characters` - which
248	would abort the queue the way 4.1 and 4.3 do. The test suite runs on SQLite, so
249	it can only pin the mismatch, not the Postgres failure.
250	
251	**Intended fix:** derive the `filename` column from the name the storage

import os
import pathlib

from django.core.exceptions import SuspiciousFileOperation


def validate_file_name(name, allow_relative_path=False):
    # Remove potentially dangerous names
    if os.path.basename(name) in {"", ".", ".."}:
        raise SuspiciousFileOperation("Could not derive file name from '%s'" % name)

    if allow_relative_path:
        # Ensure that name can be treated as a pure posix path, i.e. Unix
        # style (with forward slashes).
        path = pathlib.PurePosixPath(str(name).replace("\\", "/"))
        if path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts:
            raise SuspiciousFileOperation(
                "Detected path traversal attempt in '%s'" % name
            )
    elif name != os.path.basename(name):
        raise SuspiciousFileOperation("File name '%s' includes path elements" % name)

    return name


=== UploadedFile name setter ===
class UploadedFile(File):
    """
    An abstract uploaded file (``TemporaryUploadedFile`` and
    ``InMemoryUploadedFile`` are the built-in concrete subclasses).

    An ``UploadedFile`` object behaves somewhat like a file object and
    represents some file data that the user submitted with a form.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        file=None,
        name=None,
        content_type=None,
        size=None,
        charset=None,
        content_type_extra=None,
    ):
        super().__init__(file, name)
        self.size = size
        self.content_type = content_type
        self.charset = charset
        self.content_type_extra = content_type_extra

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<%s: %s (%s)>" % (self.__class__.__name__, self.name, self.content_type)

    def _get_name(self):
        return self._name

    def _set_name(self, name):
        # Sanitize the file name so that it can't be dangerous.
        if name is not None:
            # Just use the basename of the file -- anything else is dangerous.
            name = os.path.basename(name)

            # File names longer than 255 characters can cause problems on older OSes.
            if len(name) > 255:
                name, ext = os.path.splitext(name)
                ext = ext[:255]
                name = name[: 255 - len(ext)] + ext

            name = validate_file_name(name)

        self._name = name

class MustBeStaffMixinTests(TestCase):
    """``helpdesk/views/permissions.py`` gates the three class-based views
    through ``LoginRequiredMixin`` and ``UserPassesTestMixin``, which redirect
    from ``AccessMixin.handle_no_permission`` rather than from the
    ``user_passes_test`` wrapper the function views use. 5.2 rebuilt that
    method on ``urlsplit`` too, so it needs its own assertions.
    """

    def test_anonymous_visitor_is_sent_to_login_with_next(self):
        url = reverse("helpdesk:user_settings")
        response = self.client.get(url)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(
            response["Location"], "%s?next=%s" % (reverse("helpdesk:login"), url)
        )

    def test_authenticated_non_staff_user_is_sent_to_login_rather_than_403(self):
        User.objects.create_user(username="plain", password="pw")
        self.client.login(username="plain", password="pw")
        url = reverse("helpdesk:user_settings")
        response = self.client.get(url)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(
            response["Location"], "%s?next=%s" % (reverse("helpdesk:login"), url)
        )

    def test_staff_user_reaches_the_settings_form(self):
        staff = User.objects.create_user(username="cbvstaff", password="pw")
        staff.is_staff = True
        staff.save()
        self.client.login(username="cbvstaff", password="pw")
        response = self.client.get(reverse("helpdesk:user_settings"))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.context["form"].instance.user, staff)

263	### 4.5 A dead connection is never closed
264	
265	`pop3_sync` (`helpdesk/email.py:134-192`) calls `server.quit()` as the last
266	statement of the function, and `imap_sync` calls `expunge` / `close` / `logout`
267	at `:268-270`, all outside any `finally`. Any exception from a fetch skips them,
268	so the socket is left to the garbage collector. Harmless on a cron run that
269	exits, a slow leak in a long-lived process.
270	
271	**Intended fix:** a `try/finally` around each sync body.
272	
273	**Pinned by** the two timeout tests' closing assertions.
274	
275	### 4.6 A refused IMAP login ends the whole run, not just that queue
276	
277	`helpdesk/email.py:214` (and `:310` in `imap_oauth_sync`) calls `sys.exit()`
278	after logging an IMAP `abort`. `SystemExit` derives from `BaseException`, so
279	`process_email`'s `except Exception` at `:112` does not catch it. The loop over
280	queues dies where it stands: every queue sorted after the broken one is never
281	polled, and the management command exits non-zero.
282	
283	This is what `test_get_email.py`'s `test_get_email_with_queue_failure` believes
284	it rules out. That test raises a plain `Exception` from a mocked
285	`process_queue`, which is caught, so it passes while the real failure mode is
286	not covered.
287	
288	**Intended fix:** raise a `CommandError` (or just let the exception propagate to
289	the existing handler) instead of `sys.exit()`, so one unreachable mailbox costs
290	one queue rather than the run. Three call sites, all in `email.py`.
291	
292	**Pinned by** `test_a_refused_imap_login_stops_every_later_queue`.
293	
294	### 4.7 A queue with file logging and no previous check is never polled
295	
296	`helpdesk/email.py:91-104`:
297	
298	```python
299	if (q.logging_type in logging_types) and q.logging_dir:
300	    log_file_handler = logging.FileHandler(...)
301	    logger.addHandler(log_file_handler)
302	else:
303	    log_file_handler = None
304	    if not q.email_box_last_check:
305	        q.email_box_last_check = timezone.now() - timedelta(minutes=30)
306	try:
307	    queue_time_delta = timedelta(minutes=q.email_box_interval or 0)
308	    if (q.email_box_last_check + queue_time_delta) < timezone.now():
309	```
310	
311	The default for a null `email_box_last_check` only exists in the branch that has
312	no file handler. A queue configured with both `logging_type` and `logging_dir` -
313	the documented way to get per-queue log files - and never yet polled therefore
314	fails `:104` with
315	`TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'datetime.timedelta'`.
316	`email_box_last_check` is only written after a successful `process_queue`, so it
317	stays null and the queue fails identically forever. The only way out is to set
318	the column by hand.
319	
320	**Intended fix:** hoist the `if not q.email_box_last_check:` default above the
321	`if/else`, where it belongs - it has nothing to do with logging.
322	
323	**Pinned by** `test_a_queue_with_file_logging_and_no_previous_check_is_never_polled`.
324	
325	### 4.8 Spam checking is silently off on every install
326	
327	`helpdesk/lib.py:102-105`:
328	
329	```python
330	try:
331	    from akismet import Akismet
332	except ImportError:
333	    return False
334	```
335	
336	The version of python-akismet installed in both venvs is 25.10.1. Its
337	`akismet` package exports `SyncClient`, `AsyncClient`, `Config` and the
338	exception classes, and no `Akismet` at all - the class this import wants belongs
339	to an older API. The import therefore raises `ImportError` and `text_is_spam`
340	returns `False` unconditionally. Every
341	public ticket submission is waved through (`helpdesk/views/public.py:117`, Unit
342	5's file, is the only caller).
343	
344	The `except ImportError` was written to mean "akismet is not installed". It now
345	also swallows "akismet is installed but its API moved", and the caller cannot
346	tell a passing spam check from one that never ran. `requirements.txt:5` pins
347	`akismet` with no version at all.
348	
349	**Intended fix,** and it needs two files: rewrite `text_is_spam` against
350	`akismet.SyncClient` / `Config` (this unit's file) and give `requirements.txt` a
351	floor matching whichever release first shipped that API (**Unit 3's file**; the
352	exact version needs checking against the akismet changelog, which is not
353	available offline here). Narrowing the `except` so an installed-but-incompatible
354	akismet is loud rather than silent is the part that matters.
355	
356	**Pinned by** `test_the_installed_akismet_no_longer_exposes_the_class_lib_imports`,
357	which asserts the cause, and
358	`test_spam_checking_is_off_and_the_import_failure_is_swallowed`, which asserts
359	the effect. The first fails loudly if the dependency floor ever moves back.

362	
363	`helpdesk/lib.py:159` wraps the whole loop body in `if attached.size:`, so an
364	empty upload is neither saved nor added to the error set. `process_attachments`

Unit 5: close the last LoginRequiredMiddleware gaps in the public surface

Django 5.1's LoginRequiredMiddleware redirects every anonymous request unless
the resolved URL callback carries login_required = False, and it answers in
process_view, before helpdesk's own gate. Unit 2 opted protect_view out, which
covered the five public entry points wired through it. Six more are wired into
the URLconf bare, and all six live in this unit's files: helpdesk:submit,
helpdesk:public_change_language, kb_index, kb_category, kb_category_iframe and
kb_vote. A host project turning the middleware on loses the public submission
form, the language switcher and the whole knowledgebase to a login redirect.

Five of them now carry @login_not_required - Unit 2's guarded import, so the
attribute is set identically on 4.2 and 5.2. create_ticket still runs
protect_view internally, so the exemption hands the decision back to helpdesk's
own anonymous-access settings rather than removing it. kb.vote is deliberately
left without it: it writes, and the right answer there is a login, not an
exemption.

Nothing else in these three files needed changing. Everything they touch was
read in the installed 5.2 tree rather than recalled: View.as_view still copies
dispatch.__dict__ (the only reason @csrf_exempt on a method reaches the
middleware), CsrfViewMiddleware still reads the flag off the callback,
csrf_exempt and xframe_options_exempt were rewritten for async but still set the
same attributes in the same places, generic/base.py is byte-identical, QueryDict
is byte-identical, and HttpResponseRedirect's new second positional parameter
(preserve_request) is unreachable because every call here passes one argument.

Tests go from 10 to 72. The iframe views had two between them and neither
touched the exemptions; they now cover the submission end to end, the CSRF
exemption through a Client(enforce_csrf_checks=True) with the ordinary form as
the contrast, the validation redisplay, and framing on all four responses
dispatch can produce. Ticket lookup covers the secret-key gate in seven states
and the same lookups with HELPDESK_VIEW_A_TICKET_PUBLIC on, where the key is not
consulted at all. The knowledgebase covers a missing category and item, a
non-public category, a disabled item, and voting.

Four pre-existing bugs are pinned rather than fixed, each identical on 4.2 and
5.2, each with a comment naming it: the iframe view returns None and crashes on
a spam submission; ?queue=<slug> preselects nothing because the loop in
abstract_views overwrites the id it just looked up; /kb/<slug>/?kbitem=abc is a
500 because the except clause names only TypeError; and an anonymous visitor can
vote a KB item up without limit. A fifth, the lookup form's error message being
passed positionally and therefore dropped, is pinned too. All five are written
up in docs/migration/reports/unit-5.md with the intended fix.

        ``user_passes_test`` send the same user back to the login page. Both

Full-suite regression: 4.2 is 382 OK; 5.2 is 382 with exactly the 3 pre-existing `test_api` failures (Unit 6), unchanged from baseline.

## 3. Headline findings

**One thing the migration forced, and it is not what the brief predicted.** The iframe views' `csrf_exempt` + `xframe_options_exempt` combination is fine on 5.2 — I read `View.as_view` (byte-identical file), `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`, and both decorators (rewritten for async in 5.x, but they still set the same attributes in the same places, and `csrf_exempt` still applies `wraps` last so the flag survives). What was actually broken is Django 5.1's `LoginRequiredMiddleware`. Unit 2 opted `protect_view` out, covering the five entry points wired through it. **Six more public URLs are wired into the URLconf bare, and all six are in my files**: `helpdesk:submit`, `public_change_language`, `kb_index`, `kb_category`, `kb_category_iframe`, `kb_vote`. Five now carry `@login_not_required` (Unit 2's guarded import, so identical on 4.2). `create_ticket` still runs `protect_view` internally, so the exemption hands the decision back to helpdesk's own settings rather than removing it. `kb.vote` is deliberately left out — it writes, and the right answer there is a login; a test asserts that and a negative control proves the middleware really does take it away.

**Five pre-existing bugs pinned, not fixed** (all identical on 4.2.30 and 5.2.17, verified by probe):
- `public.py:152-154` — a spam submission through the iframe view makes `form_valid` return `None` and `xframe_options_exempt` dereference it. Crash.
- `abstract_views.py:9-13` vs `:27-28` — the by-slug queue lookup is overwritten by the raw query-string value, so `?queue=<slug>` preselects nothing and the lookup is dead code. It only works because the KB templates link with the pk.
- `kb.py:49-52` — `except TypeError` misses `ValueError`, so `/kb/<slug>/?kbitem=abc` is a 500 on a public page.
- `kb.py:83-103` — an anonymous visitor can vote a KB item up without limit; `voted_by.add(None)` is silently swallowed by `bulk_create(ignore_conflicts=True)` while the counters still move.
- `public.py:231-232` / `:249-250` — the "Missing/Invalid ticket ID" messages are passed positionally to `SearchForTicketView.as_view()`, land in `self.args`, and never reach `get_context_data`. Both messages have always been dropped.

Also noted: `USE_TZ` default flipped to `True` in 5.0 and `quicktest.py` does not set it, so rendered timestamps differ between the two runs. Both shipped settings files already set it, so this is a harness artefact only.

## 4. Left alone (other units)

- `helpdesk/tests/helpers.py` (owned by nobody): `HAS_LOGIN_REQUIRED_MIDDLEWARE` / `LOGIN_REQUIRED_MIDDLEWARE` are now defined in three test modules and the "install the middleware, one request, fresh Client" helper is written twice. Both belong there; I could not extract them. Written up as item 6 of the report.
- The three `test_api` failures on 5.2 (Unit 6).
- No `DEFAULT_FILE_STORAGE` problem surfaced — Unit 8 has already landed.
